# Using Google Tag Manager to Install the Appier Web SDK

You can install the Appier Web SDK in your website’s pages via GTM. Doing this also enables you to check if tags are being fired from your website.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note:
> 
> Before adding web SDK code via GTM, you need to go to [AIQUA Dashboard](https://aiqua.appier.com/setup/website) to complete the following steps:
> 
>   1. Enter website information.
>   2. Add `qg-sw.<your-app-id>.js` file to the website's root directory. See [here](doc:integrating-with-the-aiqua-web-sdk#section-part-ii-integrate-sdk).
> 


## 

Implementing GTM on Your Website

Skip this section if you have already implemented GTM on your website.

  1. Sign in to Google Tag Manager and click **Create Account**.
  2. Under **Add a New Account** , input all the needed details and select **Web** as the location of your container setup.

![](https://files.readme.io/d3a547f-GTM_step_2.png)

  3. Click **Create**.
  4. Go through the Google Tag Manager Terms of Service Agreement, tick the box to agree, then click **Yes** to proceed.
  5. Follow the onscreen instructions on **Install Google Tag Manager** and install the GTM code in all of your website pages.

![](https://files.readme.io/990f8e2-GTM_step_5.PNG)

## 

Adding Appier Web SDK Code via GTM

  1. On GTM, go to **Workspace** to create a custom tag.
  2. Click **Tags > New**.

![](https://files.readme.io/9a4b010-gtm_step_7.PNG)

  3. Do the following in the pop-up screen:

a. Click **Untitled Tag** and rename it.

b. Click the edit icon in Tag Configuration then select **Custom HTML**


![](https://files.readme.io/1791665-gtm_step_8.png)

c. In the HTML body, copy and paste the Appier Web code.

![](https://files.readme.io/e2b1384-gtm_step_8b.png)   


> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note:
> 
> Retrieve this code by going to the **AIQUA Dashboard > Your account name > Integration >[Web](https://aiqua.appier.com/setup/website)**. If your website info is already entered, click **Next** then scroll down to **3\. ADD FOLLOWING LINES TO INDEX.HTML**.

![](https://files.readme.io/cfc7a96-web-install-sdk.png)

d. Click the edit icon in **Triggering** then select **All Pages** to implement personalization features in your website. This also allows you to set up different rules for firing tags according to your use case.

![](https://files.readme.io/9760794-gtm_step_8d1.png) ![](https://files.readme.io/d8d45bc-gtm_step_8d2.PNG)

e. Click **Save**.

  4. Click **Preview** and go to your website. The debug mode appears on the bottom of the browser window to let you check if tags are firing properly from your website.

![](https://files.readme.io/660b630-9-1_edited.png) ![](https://files.readme.io/6a8882f-9-2_edited.png)

  5. When you’re done checking, click **Submit > Publish**.

![](https://files.readme.io/ce299e5-10-1.png) ![](https://files.readme.io/2039729-10-2.png)

# Installing the iOS SDK

Install the Appier iOS SDK using one of the following methods:

  * Installing with Swift Package Manager
  * Installing with CocoaPods
  * Manual installation (Not recommended)



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * **iOS apps using Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)** : You must integrate the Firebase SDK to your app in addition to the Appier iOS SDK.
> 
>   * **Using a new notification service** : If your app is already integrated with Apple Push Notification service (APNs), all of your existing iOS push subscribers will be lost if you switch to FCM. The same applies when switching your notification service from FCM to APNs.
> 
>   * **Location tracking** : AIQUA only tracks location if you properly initialize location services. Remember to add any key(s) required for [requesting authorization for location services](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corelocation/requesting_authorization_for_location_services) in `info.plist`.
> 
> 


* * *

## 

Installing with Swift Package Manager

### 

Xcode 12.5.1 or earlier

  1. Open your Xcode project and select **File > Swift Packages > Add Package Dependency**.
  2. Input the following repository URL: `https://github.com/appier/appier-ios-framework`, then click **Next**.
  3. For **Rules** , select **Version** and choose **Up to Next Major** and set the version number to `7.17.0` or later. We recommend using the latest version of the Appier iOS SDK, version `<<latest_ios_sdk_version>>`.

![497](https://files.readme.io/d9aad40-ios-sdk-using-spm-add-package-dependency_1.png)

  4. In the next screen, under **Package Product** , select `AppierFramework`. If you plan to use push notifications, select `AppierExtensionFramework` as well.

![535](https://files.readme.io/d913544-ios-sdk-add-packages.png)

  5. Click **Finish** to complete the installation.



For more details about adding dependencies, see Apple's documentation on [Adding Package Dependencies to Your App](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swift_packages/adding_package_dependencies_to_your_app).

### 

Xcode 13 or later

  1. Open your Xcode project and select **File > Add Packages**.
  2. In the search bar, enter the following package URL: `https://github.com/appier/appier-ios-framework`

![1114](https://files.readme.io/ae2090c-xcode_add_appier_sdk.png)

  3. For **Dependency Rule** , choose **Up to Next Major** and set the version number to `7.17.0` or later. We recommend using the latest version of the Appier iOS SDK, version `<<latest_ios_sdk_version>>`.

![1112](https://files.readme.io/e394281-xcode_add_appier_sdk_dependency_rule.png)

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> `artifact not found for target "AppierFramework"`
> 
> This error may occur for apps using **iOS SDK 7.17.0 or earlier** and developing on **Xcode 13.3 or later** because Swift Package Manager (SPM) requires the artifact name to match the target name.
> 
> If you encounter this error, set `appier-ios-framework`'s **Dependency Rule** to **Branch** with the branch name set to `master`.

  4. In the next screen, under **Package Product** , select `AppierFramework`. If you plan to use push notifications, select `AppierExtensionFramework` as well.

![685](https://files.readme.io/47e2409-xcode_add_packages.png)

  5. Click **Add Package** to complete the installation.



* * *

## 

Installing with Cocoapods

### 

Prerequisites

  1. Install CocoaPods version 1.10.0 or later
  2. Create a Podfile



For instructions on completing these steps, see the [CocoaPods Getting Started guide](https://guides.cocoapods.org/using/getting-started.html).

### 

1\. Add the Appier SDK pod to your Podfile

Add the `AppierFramework` dependency to your Podfile. We recommend using the latest version of the Appier SDK, version 8.6.0.

Podfile (SDK 7.0.0 or above)
    
    
    target 'PROJECT_TARGET' do
      ...
      # Add the pod for the Appier SDK
      pod 'AppierFramework', '<<latest_ios_sdk_version>>'
    
    end

### 

2\. Create your workspace

  1. In the project directory, run the following commands to install the dependencies and create a new workspace:
         
         $ pod repo update
         $ pod install

  2. Open the `PROJECT_TARGET.xcworkspace` file created by CocoaPods.


![](https://files.readme.io/2a3f461-Screen_Shot_2020-06-02_at_8.21.46_AM.png)

  3. (For Objective C only): Go to **Build Settings > Build Options** and make sure **Always Embed Swift Standard Libraries** is set to **Yes**.

![](https://files.readme.io/c3a413a-Screen_Shot_2020-08-25_at_4.14.07_PM.png)

### 

Usage

Import the following header to use the Appier Framework:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    import Appier
    
    
    #import <Appier/Appier.h>

* * *

## 

Manual installation (Not recommended)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> For React Native or Flutter projects, you don't need to install the Appier iOS SDK in the main app target.

  1. Download the SDK file listed on the [AIQUA iOS SDK Integration Overview](doc:ios-sdk-integration-overview#latest-ios-sdk-version) page.
  2. Add the downloaded **Appier.xcframework** folder to your main app target. Go to **Build Phases > Link Binary With Libraries**, click **+** , then select **Add Other...** > **Add Files...** and choose the `Appier.xcframework` folder.

![](https://files.readme.io/2281d02-Screen_Shot_2020-08-25_at_4.51.43_PM.png) ![815](https://files.readme.io/540f59c-Screen_Shot_2021-04-19_at_5.13.26_PM.png)

  3. (For Objective-C only) Go to **Build Settings > Build Options** and make sure **Always Embed Swift Standard Libraries** is set to **Yes**.

![](https://files.readme.io/5e55b33-Screen_Shot_2020-08-25_at_4.14.07_PM.png)

  4. Go to **General > Frameworks, Libraries, and Embedded Content**, select `Appier.xcframework` and set the **Embed** option to **Embed & Sign**.

![](https://files.readme.io/492be4d-Appier.xcframework.png)

  5. Import the following header to use the Appier Framework:



SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    import Appier
    
    
    #import <Appier/Appier.h>

# Installing the SDK via pub.dev

First, add dependency in `Pubspec.yaml`:

Pubspec.yaml
    
    
    dependencies:
      ...
      appier_flutter: <<latest_flutter_sdk_version>>

And then pull the package by running `flutter pub get`:

Shell
    
    
    $ flutter pub get

# Installing the SDK via React Native

Refer to the following methods when integrating the Appier Enterprise Service SDK ("Appier SDK") using React Native.

## 

1\. Installation

npmyarn
    
    
    $ npm install @appier/react-native-sdk --save
    
    
    $ yarn add @appier/react-native-sdk

After installing the SDK, it needs to be linked to native Android and iOS libraries. Follow the below section based on the React Native version you are using.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Web views
> 
> If you need to log custom data from app web views, you'll also need to install `react-native-webview`. Refer to [React Native SDK Web View Support](doc:react-native-webview-support) for details.

* * *

## 

2\. Link native modules in React Native

### 

React Native 0.60.0 or later

Automatic linking is supported for Appier React Native SDK versions 1.3.1 or later.

#### 

**Android**

All the dependencies should be automatically added. In case of issues, refer to Gradle files in Android Studio.

#### 

**iOS**

[Install the Appier iOS SDK via CocoaPods](doc:rich-push-notifications-react-native#installing-with-cocoapods).

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note:
> 
> In a later step, you'll need to use the same **Podfile** created to add Notification Service Extension and Notification Content Extension targets and their dependency for `AppierFramework`. This dependency will be managed by `node_modules` for the **main app target** in iOS.

### 

React Native 0.46.0 to 0.59.10

react-native
    
    
    $ react-native link @appier/react-native-sdk

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Manual linking
> 
> Manual linking is not recommended, but if needed, follow the instructions described in Manual linking.

* * *

## 

Manual linking

### 

Android

  1. Open up `android/app/src/main/java/[...]/MainActivity.java` then add `import com.reactlibrary.RNAiquaSdkPackage;` to the imports at the top of the file.
  2. Add the new `RNAiquaSdkPackage()` to the list returned by the `getPackages()` method.
  3. Append the following lines to `android/settings.gradle`:



settings.gradle
    
    
    include ':appier_react-native-sdk' project(':appier_react-native-sdk').projectDir = new File(rootProject.projectDir, '../node_modules/@appier/react-native-sdk/android')

  4. Insert the following lines inside the dependencies block in `android/app/build.gradle`:



build.gradle
    
    
    implementation project(':appier_react-native-sdk')

### 

iOS

  1. In Xcode, go to the project navigator then right-click `Libraries` **>** `Add Files to [your project's name]`.
  2. Go to `node_modules` **>** `@appier/react-native-sdk` and add `RNAiquaSdk.xcodeproj`.
  3. In Xcode, go to the project navigator then select your project. Add `libRNAiquaSdk.a` to your project's `Build Phases` **>** `Link Binary With Libraries`.
  4. Run your project using `(Cmd+R)<`.

# Integrating Shopify Stores with the Appier Web SDK

## 

Overview

Integrate the Web SDK with your Shopify store to begin leveraging AIQUA features such as collecting user events and attributes, sending campaigns, and displaying product recommendations.

  * Supported features: View the list of supported AIQUA features.
  * User data collection: Understand what type of data the Web SDK can collect from your Shopify store.



> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Integration using `checkout.liquid`
> 
> If you've previously integrated the Web SDK using `checkout.liquid`, please follow these steps:
> 
>   1. Follow the instructions in Shopify’s [Checkout Extensibility upgrade guide](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/checkout-settings/customize-checkout-configurations/checkout-extensibility).
>   2. Proceed directly to Install the purchase tracking code (checkout events) for instructions on replacing the `checkout.liquid` event tracking code with a custom pixel.
> 


### 

Supported features

The following table summarizes AIQUA features supported in Shopify stores. Note that the scope of support differs between the sandbox environment for pixels and unsandboxed environments, due to Shopify's sandbox environment limitations.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Sandbox environment for pixels
> 
> On August 13, 2024, `checkout.liquid` will be deprecated for Information, Shipping, and Payment pages, and will be replaced with [Checkout Extensibility](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/checkout-settings/customize-checkout-configurations/checkout-extensibility#upgrade-extensibility).
> 
> After this change, the Information, Shipping, and Payment pages will run in a sandboxed environment, limiting third-party access to page data, including user events, and will require [pixels](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/pixels/overview#pixels-sandbox-environment) to track event data.

Feature| Supported (unsandboxed environments)| Supported (sandboxed environment for pixels)  
---|---|---  
Audience segmentation| Yes| Yes  
Campaign-related features| • Regular campaigns: Yes (excluding app push)  
• Trigger campaigns: Yes (excluding app push)  
• In-Web Campaigns: Yes  
• Creative Studio: Yes  
• Journey Maps: Yes  
• Experiment: Yes| No  
Performance and analytics| Yes| No  
Recommendations| Yes| No  
Dynamic content| Yes| No  
  
### 

User data collection

After installing the general tracking code, the Web SDK automatically collects [default events and attributes](doc:default-aiqua-parameters)—no additional code changes are required. In addition, the following custom events and attributes will automatically be collected as well:

Type| Name| Description  
---|---|---  
Attribute| `email`| The email address of the user who logged in.  
Attribute| `phoneNo`| The phone number of the user who logged in.  
Attribute| `first_name`| The first name of the user who logged in.  
Attribute| `last_name`| The last name of the user who logged in.  
Event| `searched`| Generated when the user searches a keyword on the website.  
Event| `category_viewed`| Generated when the user views a product category page on the website.  
Event| `product_viewed`| Generated when the user views a product page on the website.  
Event| `product_added_to_cart`| Generated when the user adds a product to the shopping cart on the website.  
  
> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> To collect custom data not listed in the table above, you can implement your own custom event collection using the Web SDK logging methods in the general tracking code. Refer to the following guides to learn more about logging custom data:
> 
>   * [Guidelines for Logging Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data)
>   * [Logging User Attributes for Web](doc:logging-profile-information-on-the-web-sdk)
>   * [Logging User Events for Web](doc:logging-event-information-on-the-web-sdk)
>

## 

1\. Register your website on the AIQUA dashboard

  1. Click on your account name in the lower-left corner of the AIQUA dashboard and select [**Integration > Website**](https://aiqua.appier.com/setup/website).

![](https://files.readme.io/3ad51b6-nav-web-integration.png)

  2. Enter the URL of your Shopify store and configure the following options.
     1. Check **Enable Web Push** to enable web push notifications. If you want to restrict web push to specific URLs only, select **Restrict web push in specific websites only** and enter the websites you want to allow web push notifications for.
     2. Check **Enable In-Web Notification** if you want to enable AIQUA's in-web campaigns.

![](https://files.readme.io/b7f56e6-web-website-info.png)

  3. Click **Next** to save your settings.

![](https://files.readme.io/f5efa62-web-website-info-save.png)

* * *

## 

2\. Install AIQUA Notify on Shopify

  1. Log in to Shopify dashboard and copy the `".myshopify.com"` URL of your shop.
  2. Share your Shopify URL with Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#224751517d515752524d5056624352524b47500c414d4f)), who will provide you with a link where you can install the AIQUA Notify app.

![](https://files.readme.io/8214b5d-Shopify_AIQUA_notify.png)

  3. After installing the AIQUA Notify app, contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#ee8b9d9db19d9b9e9e819c9aae8f9e9e878b9cc08d8183)) to complete the setup process.

![](https://files.readme.io/fc98a05-Screen_Shot_2022-02-22_at_2.23.24_PM.png)   


* * *

## 

3\. Install the Appier Web SDK

Next, install the general tracking code and purchase tracking code:

  1. Installing the general tracking code will begin collection of default data and the specified custom data.
  2. Installing the purchase tracking code (checkout events) will begin collecting checkout events.



### 

Install the general tracking code

  1. On Shopify dashboard, go to **Online Store > Themes**, click the actions button (three horizontal dots) on the theme you want to use, and select **Edit code**.

![](https://files.readme.io/e69ea36-shopify-3-1.png)

  2. In the code editor, select **Snippets** and click **Add a new snippet**.

![](https://files.readme.io/c1cd2e8-shopify-3-2.png)

  3. Name the snippet "aiqua-track" and click **Done**.

![](https://files.readme.io/6c2cfa7-shopify-3-3.png)

  4. Go to `aiqua-track.liquid` in the menu, and paste the following code:



aiqua-track.liquid
    
    
    <!-- Start AIQUA Tracking Code -->
    {% unless appierRtAddToCartSelector %}
      {% assign appierRtAddToCartSelector = 'YOUR-ADD-TO-CART-BUTTON-SELECTOR' %}
    {% endunless %}
    
    <script>
      function fixPriceForAiqua(price) {
        let appierRtPrice = price;
        const appierRtPriceCommas = appierRtPrice.match(/,/g);
        if (appierRtPriceCommas && appierRtPriceCommas.length === 1 && /,[0-9]{0,2}$/.test(appierRtPrice)) {
          appierRtPrice = appierRtPrice.replaceAll('.', '').replace(',', '.');
        } else {
          appierRtPrice = appierRtPrice.replace(',', '');
        }
        return parseFloat(appierRtPrice);
      }
    </script>
    
    <script>  
      !function(q,g,r,a,p,h,js) {
        q.appier=q.qg
        if(q.qg)return;
        js=q.appier=q.qg=function() {
          js.callmethod ? js.callmethod.call(js, arguments) : js.queue.push(arguments);
        };
        js.queue=[];
        p=g.createElement(r);p.async=!0;p.src=a;h=g.getElementsByTagName(r)[0];
        h.parentNode.insertBefore(p,h);
      } (window,document,"script","https://cdn.qgr.ph/qgraph.{{appid}}.js");
    </script>
    
     
    <!-- Begin Appier Login tag -->
    {% if customer %} 
      <script>
        appier("identify", {
          email: "{{ customer.email }}",
          phoneNo: "{{ customer.phone }}",
          first_name: "{{ customer.first_name }}",
          last_name: "{{ customer.last_name }}"
        });
      </script>
    {% endif %}
    <!-- End Appier Login tag -->
    
    <!-- Begin Appier Search Tag -->
    {% if request.page_type == 'search' %}
      {% if search.performed == true %}
      <script>
        const appierRtSearch = "{{ search.terms }}".split(" ");
        appier("event", "searched", {
          searched_keyword: appierRtSearch
        });
      </script>
      {% endif %}
    {% endif %}
    <!-- End Appier Search Tag -->
    
    <!-- Begin Appier Product Category tag -->
    {% if request.page_type == 'collection' %}
      <script>
        var appierRtCategory = [];
        {% for product_type in collection.all_types %}
            if ("{{product_type}}") {
                appierRtCategory.push("{{product_type}}");
            }
        {% endfor %}
        var category = appierRtCategory.join(",");
        
        appier("event", "category_viewed", {
          category_name: category
        });
      </script>
    {% endif %}
    <!-- End Appier Product Category tag -->
    
    <!-- Begin Appier Product View tag -->
    {% if request.page_type == 'product' %}
      <script>
        appier("event", "product_viewed", {
          product_id: "{{ product.id }}",
          product_price: fixPriceForAiqua("{{ product.price | money_without_currency }}"),
          category_name: "{{ product.type }}",
          product_url: "{{shop.secure_url}}" + "{{product.url}}",
          product_image_url: "https:" + "{{ product | img_url }}"
        });
      </script>
    {% endif %}
    <!-- End Appier Product View tag -->
    
    <!-- Begin Appier Add to Cart Tag -->
    <script>
      window.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
        document.querySelectorAll('{{ appierRtAddToCartSelector }}').forEach( function(node){
          node.addEventListener("click", function() {
            appier("event", "product_added_to_cart", {
              product_id: "{{ product.id }}",
              product_price: fixPriceForAiqua("{{ product.price | money_without_currency }}"),
              category_name: "{{ product.type }}",
              product_url: "{{shop.secure_url}}" + "{{product.url}}",
              product_image_url: "https:" + "{{ product | img_url }}"
            });                                                
          });    
        });
      });
    </script>
    <!-- End Appier Add to Cart Tag -->
    
    <!-- END AIQUA Tracking Code -->
    

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Custom data
> 
> To collect other custom events and attributes, you can implement your own custom event collection using the Web SDK logging methods in the general tracking code. Refer to the following guides to learn more about logging custom data:
> 
>   * [Guidelines for Logging Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data)
>   * [Logging User Attributes for Web](doc:logging-profile-information-on-the-web-sdk)
>   * [Logging User Events for Web](doc:logging-event-information-on-the-web-sdk)
> 


  5. In `aiqua-track.liquid`, search for `{{ YOUR-ADD-TO-CART-BUTTON-SELECTOR }}` and replace it with the class name of the add-to-cart button. Since Shopify offers different kinds of buttons, this step identifies which buttons are the add-to-cart buttons on your Shopify site. To find the button's class name:
     1. Right-click the add-to-cart button and select **Inspect** or **Inspect Elements**.
     2. Find the class name of the button, and copy a unique part of the class name.
     3. Replace all instances of `{{ YOUR-ADD-TO-CART-BUTTON-SELECTOR }}` in the code snippet with the class name you copied.

![](https://files.readme.io/7047b5b-shopify-button-class-name.png)

  6. Click **Save**.
  7. In the left menu of the code editor, select **Layout** and click `theme.liquid`.

![](https://files.readme.io/415c99b-Screen_Shot_2022-02-23_at_5.21.48_PM.png)

  8. Add the following code snippet into the `<head>` element of `theme.liquid`, replacing `{{ YOUR_APP_ID }}` with your AIQUA app ID, then click **Save**.



Inside theme.liquid
    
    
    {% render 'aiqua-track' , appid: '{{ YOUR_APP_ID }}' %}

![](https://files.readme.io/dd16348-theme-liquid-code.png)

  9. Repeat steps 1-8 for each theme you want to use.



### 

Install the purchase tracking code (checkout events)

The Web SDK uses custom pixels to track events. The following section provides instructions on creating a custom pixel for the checkout event and its associated tracking code.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> To learn more about managing your custom pixels, see [Shopify's custom pixel guide](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/pixels/custom-pixels/manage).

On Shopify dashboard, go to **Settings** , click **Customer events** in the left menu, then **Add custom pixel**.

![](https://files.readme.io/31b92a9-shopify-add-custom-pixel.png)

Enter a name for the custom pixel, then click **Add pixel**.

![](https://files.readme.io/c1da086-shopify-add-pixel.png)

Next, install code snippets in the **Code** section to:

  1. Initialize the JavaScript Pixel SDK.
  2. Subscribe to customer events.



#### 

Initialize the JavaScript pixel SDK

Initialize the pixel SDK. Replace `{app_id}` with your AIQUA app ID.

JavaScript
    
    
    // Step 1. Initialize the JavaScript pixel SDK (make sure to exclude HTML)
    !(function (q, g, r, a, p, h, js) {
      // Initialize Appier SDK only in the checkout process
      const isCheckoutProcess = /\/checkouts(?:\/|$)/.test(
        window.location.pathname
      );
      if (!isCheckoutProcess) return;
      q.appier = q.qg;
      if (q.qg) return;
      js = q.appier = q.qg = function () {
        js.callmethod ? js.callmethod.call(js, arguments) : js.queue.push(arguments);
      };
      js.queue = [];
      p = g.createElement(r);
      p.async = !0;
      p.src = a;
      h = g.getElementsByTagName(r)[0];
      h.parentNode.insertBefore(p, h);
    })(window,document,'script','https://cdn.qgr.ph/qgraph.{app_id}.js');
    
    // Helper function for normalizing price format
    function fixPriceForAiqua(price) {
      let appierRtPrice = price.toString();
      const appierRtPriceCommas = appierRtPrice.match(/,/g);
      if (
        appierRtPriceCommas &&
        appierRtPriceCommas.length === 1 &&
        /,[0-9]{0,2}$/.test(appierRtPrice)
      ) {
        appierRtPrice = appierRtPrice.replaceAll('.', '').replace(',', '.');
      } else {
        appierRtPrice = appierRtPrice.replace(',', '');
      }
      return parseFloat(appierRtPrice);
    }

#### 

Subscribe to customer events

Subscribe to customer events with `analytics.subscribe()` and add tracking code for the checkout event (`checkout_completed`). After installing the following code snippet, [checkout events and their properties](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/web-pixels-api/standard-events/checkout_completed) will be logged to AIQUA.

JavaScript
    
    
    // Step 2. Subscribe to customer events with analytics.subscribe(), and add tracking
    //  analytics.subscribe("all_standard_events", event => {
    //    console.log("Event data ", event?.data);
    //  });
    
    // checkout_completed
    analytics.subscribe('checkout_completed', (event) => {
      const checkout = event.data.checkout;
      const lineItems = checkout.lineItems;
      lineItems.forEach((item) => {
        const itemPrice = item.variant.price.amount;
        // Log event `product_purchased` to Appier
        appier?.('event', 'product_purchased', {
          order_id: checkout.order.id,
          product_id: item.id,
          product_url: `${event.context.document.location.origin}${item.variant.product.url}`,
          product_name: item.title,
          product_price: fixPriceForAiqua(itemPrice),
          quantity: item.quantity,
        }, fixPriceForAiqua(itemPrice));
      });
    
      const orderPrice = fixPriceForAiqua(event.data.checkout.subtotalPrice.amount);
      // Log event `checkout_completed` to Appier
      appier?.('event', 'checkout_completed', {
          order_id: event.data.checkout.order.id,
          order_price: orderPrice,
        },
        orderPrice
      );
    });

4\. Verify the integration

Follow the steps below to verify that events and attributes are being collected by the Web SDK.

  1. On the AIQUA dashboard, click your account name in the lower-left corner, and select **Recent Activity** to see collected user events or select **Recent Users** to see collected user attributes.
  2. Click the **Web** tab to see events or attributes collected from your Shopify site.

# Custom Web View Implementation

## 

Overview

You can inject custom JavaScript into your own web view implementation to track custom events and attributes logged from a web view. If you don't need a custom web view implementation, we recommend [using the `QGWKWebView` class](doc:ios-webview-support) to configure WebView logging, as `QGWKWebView` is continually updated to support new features.

### 

Requirements and limitations

  * Ensure your app uses SDK v7.28.0 or later before implementing a custom web view.
  * The [Web SDK's default user events and attributes](doc:default-aiqua-parameters) (such as `page_viewed` and `visited`) aren't logged from within a web view.



* * *

## 

Integration guide

### 

1\. Inject the AIQUA script

Use `WKUserScript` to inject AIQUA's script as soon as the `WKWebView` instance is loaded.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    let userScript = WKUserScript(source: QGWKWebViewUserScript, injectionTime: .atDocumentStart, forMainFrameOnly: false)
    // add the user script to the webview user controller
    webview.configuration.userContentController.addUserScript(userScript)
    
    
    WKUserScript *aiqUserScript = [[WKUserScript alloc] initWithSource:QGWKWebViewUserScript
                                                         injectionTime:WKUserScriptInjectionTimeAtDocumentStart
                                                      forMainFrameOnly:NO];
    // add the user script to the webview user controller
    [self.webView.configuration.userContentController addUserScript:aiqUserScript];

### 

2\. Implement a native interface

To invoke the native iOS code from JavaScript code, create a message handler class conforming to the `WKScriptMessageHandler` protocol. The message body contains the data to be sent.

Use the following code sample containing `handleScriptMessage()`/`handleScriptMessageOfWebView()`—these methods contain the message handling implementation and greatly simplifies the required code:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    func userContentController(_ userContentController: WKUserContentController,
                               didReceive message: WKScriptMessage) {
      if message.name == "aiqua" {
        QGSdk.getSharedInstance().handleScriptMessage(of: self,
                                                      userContentController: userContentController,
                                                      didReceive: message)
      } else {
        // handle other messages
      }
    }
    
    
    - (void)userContentController:(nonnull WKUserContentController *)userContentController
          didReceiveScriptMessage:(nonnull WKScriptMessage *)message {
        if ([message.name isEqualToString: @"aiqua"]) {
            [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] handleScriptMessageOfWebView:self
                                              userContentController:userContentController
                                            didReceiveScriptMessage:message];
        } else {
            // handle other messages
            NSLog(@"received message %@", message.name);
        }
    }

Finally, add the message handler to the web view's user content controller:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    self.webview.configuration.userContentController.add(self, name: "aiqua")
    
    
    [self.webView.configuration.userContentController addScriptMessageHandler:self name:@"aiqua"];

### 

3\. Verify your web view integration

Launch your web view and verify that events and attributes are logged in the [Recent Activity](https://aiqua.appier.com/recent_activity) or [Recent Users](https://aiqua.appier.com/recent_users) section of the AIQUA dashboard.

# Production and Development Environments

## 

Overview

When integrating your app with the iOS SDK, it's important to take note of which environment you're using for push notification to be sent properly.

In the following diagram, we see that depending on the debug/release build configurations you have for your app, user data – including push permission tokens – are stored in separate databases on AIQUA and Apple Push Notification service (APNs).

![](https://files.readme.io/2f9ab0f-Screen_Shot_2020-06-16_at_9.55.49_AM.png)

The following sections describe points in the SDK integration process when you'll need to ensure that your environment configuration is correct.

* * *

## 

Initializing the SDK

The code for [initializing the iOS SDK](doc:initializing-the-ios-sdk) already includes a flag that conditionally sets the value of the `setDevProfile` parameter based on the app's build configuration. If you choose to not use the flag, note that:

  * If `setDevProfile` is `true`, the user data will only be sent to the Dev DB.
  * If `setDevProfile` is `false`, the user data will only be sent to the Prod DB.



* * *

## 

Generating a push certificate

When [configuring iOS push certificates](doc:creating-push-certificates), if you're using .p12 files, you need to upload separate .p12 certificates for the two environments. If you're using .p8 files, only one certificate is needed for both environments.

* * *

## 

Configuring Xcode project settings

### 

APS environment entitlement

The APS environment key specifies which Apple Push Notification service (APNs) environment to use when registering for push notifications.

In your project's root directory, open the `.entitlements` file and verify that the value of **APS Environment** corresponds to the environment you're developing for – either `production` or `development`.

![](https://files.readme.io/38c2053-aps-environment-entitlement.png)

See [Apple's docs on the APS Environment Entitlement](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/entitlements/aps-environment) for details.

### 

Build configuration

When you're ready to build and run your app, go to Xcode, click the build scheme, and select **Edit Scheme**. Use the **Build Configuration** drop-down list to select **Debug** or **Release** mode.

![](https://files.readme.io/cb07bff-xcode_2.gif)

* * *

## 

Sending campaigns

When sending an iOS campaign from the AIQUA dashboard, you need to select whether you're using the **Production profile** or **Development profile** based on the app's build configuration. If the wrong profile is selected, the push notification won't be delivered.

![](https://files.readme.io/6fe80a55691f0594835fc491213e7583f18b49da6f41062df72fa63a20564562-Sending_iOS_test_notification.png)

* * *

## 

Accessing data on AIQUA dashboard

The following pages on the AIQUA dashboard list production and development environment data separately:

  * **Account name > Recent users**
  * **Account name > Recent activity**
  * **Audiences > Segment list**
  * **Analytics**



Data sent to the Dev DB can be seen under the **iOS development** , while data sent to the Prod DB can be seen under **iOS production**.

![](https://files.readme.io/0c7b8ac-ios-production-development_1.png)

__Updated 9 months ago

* * *

# Adding Required Extensions

## 

Overview

This guide will explain how to add the **Notification Service Extension** and **Notification Content Extension** to your app. These extensions are required for:

  1. **Tracking impressions for push notifications** : Tracking impression events for push notifications is only possible after the extensions are added.
  2. **Sending rich push notifications** : A rich push notification is a push notification that includes an image, video, GIF, audio, carousel, or slider. With the release of iOS 10, `AppierFramework` and `AppierExtensionFramework` were introduced to support rich push notifications and notification UI customization.



### 

SDK version requirement

We recommend using **Appier iOS SDK 7.10.0 or later**. Follow the [migration steps](doc:migrating-to-ios-sdk-700) to upgrade from version 7.0.0-7.9.0. If you're using an earlier version, please note the following:

  * If you're using a new App Group ID, ensure that you are using **Appier iOS SDK 7.7.0** or later, otherwise iOS users will be duplicated.
  * Starting from **Appier iOS SDK 8.0.0** , `AppierFramework` is not supported in the Notification Service Extension and Notification Content Extension.
  * Starting from **Appier iOS SDK 7.10.0** , `AppierExtensionFramework` is used in the Notification Service Extension and Notification Content Extension. `AppierFramework` is only used in the main app target.



* * *

## 

1\. Save your App Group ID

The App Group ID will be used in your main app target as well as the two extension targets you'll create. The App Group ID must be the same ID used when you [enabled the App Group](doc:enabling-capabilities).

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Caution: Using a New App Group ID
> 
> Ensure that you're using the proper SDK version if you need to use a new App Group ID to avoid unwanted side effects.

![](https://files.readme.io/b86ff42-step-1-1.png)

* * *

## 

2\. Add the extensions

  1. Add a notification service extension target. Under to **File > New > Target**, select **Notification Service Extension** , then click **Next**.

![](https://files.readme.io/75da0f8-step-2-1.png)

  2. For **Product Name** , enter "AppierNotificationServiceExtension" and click **Finish**.

![](https://files.readme.io/8a3e66e-step-2-2.png)

  3. After clicking **Finish** , you'll be prompted to activate the "AppierNotificationServiceExtension" scheme. Select **Cancel**.

![](https://files.readme.io/83b663a-step-2-3.png)

  4. Add a notification content extension target. In Xcode, navigate to **File > New > Target**, select **Notification Content Extension** , and click **Next**.

![](https://files.readme.io/5fcbfa1-step-2-4.png)

  5. For **Product Name** , enter "AppierNotificationContentExtension" and click **Finish**.

![](https://files.readme.io/78a53b9-step-2-5.png)

  6. After clicking **Finish** , you'll be prompted to activate the "AppierNotificationContentExtension" scheme. Select **Cancel**.

![](https://files.readme.io/a33f59f-step-2-6.png)

* * *

## 

3\. Install the extensions

Choose an installation method depending on your project settings:

  * **Option 1** : Installing with Swift Package Manager
  * **Option 2** : Installing with CocoaPods
  * **Option 3** : Manual Installation (Not Recommended)



### 

Swift Package Manager

No additional steps required; continue to the next step.

### 

Installing with CocoaPods

#### 

Update Your Podfile

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> use_frameworks!
> 
> Your Podfile will look different depending on whether it contains `use_frameworks!` or not. Make sure you are referencing the correct Podfile sample.

If your Podfile has `use_frameworks!`, add the following lines to your Podfile:

Ruby
    
    
    platform :ios, '10.0'
    use_frameworks!
    
    target 'PROJECT_TARGET' do
      pod 'AppierFramework', '<<latest_ios_sdk_version>>'
      # other pods
    end
    
    # Add the following lines for service and content extensions
    target 'AppierNotificationServiceExtension' do
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<<latest_ios_sdk_version>>'
    end
    
    target 'AppierNotificationContentExtension' do
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<<latest_ios_sdk_version>>'
    end

Otherwise, add the following lines to your Podfile instead:

Ruby
    
    
    platform :ios, '10.0'
    
    target 'PROJECT_TARGET' do
      pod 'AppierFramework', '<<latest_ios_sdk_version>>'
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<<latest_ios_sdk_version>>'
      # other pods
    end
    
    # Add the following lines for service and content extensions
    target 'AppierNotificationServiceExtension' do
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<<latest_ios_sdk_version>>'
    end
    
    target 'AppierNotificationContentExtension' do
      pod 'AppierExtensionFramework', '<<latest_ios_sdk_version>>'
    end

Ensure that the target names in the Podfile match the product names you used when creating the extensions (`AppierNotificationServiceExtension` and `AppierNotificationContentExtension`).

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Upgrading the iOS SDK
> 
> When upgrading the iOS SDK, make sure to also update the versions of `AppierExtensionFramework` and `AppierFramework` in your Podfile to match the iOS SDK version.

#### 

Install the Extensions

After adding the extensions to the Podfile, run the following commands in the project directory to install the extensions:

Shell
    
    
    $ pod repo update
    $ pod install

### 

Manual installation (not recommended)

> ❗️
> 
> ### 
> 
> Warning
> 
> Don't follow the manual installation steps if your project uses CocoaPods or Swift Package Manager (SPM) for package management.

  1. [Download the Appier iOS SDK](doc:ios-sdk-integration-overview).
  2. Add the `AppierExtension.xcframework` folder you downloaded to the main app target. Under the **Build Phases** tab, expand **Link Binary With Libraries** , and click **+**. Go to **Add Other > Add Files** and select the `AppierExtension.xcframework` folder.

![Add the AppierExtension.xcframework folder to the main app target.](https://files.readme.io/6593dc4-Screen_Shot_2021-09-15_at_12.40.08_PM.png)

  3. Add the `AppierExtension.xcframework` folder to the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** and **AppierNotificationContentExtension** targets.

![Add the AppierExtension.xcframework folder to the AppierNotificationServiceExtension and AppierNotificationContentExtension targets.](https://files.readme.io/8e7e76a-Screen_Shot_2020-08-27_at_2.12.13_PM.png)

  4. In the main app target, go to **General > Frameworks and Libraries**, select `AppierExtension.xcframework`, and set the **Embed** column to **Embed & Sign**.

![](https://files.readme.io/3d26c88-manual-installation_main_app_target_embed_setting.png)

  5. In the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** and **AppierNotificationContentExtension** targets, go to **General > Frameworks and Libraries**, then set the **Embed** columns of `AppierNotificationServiceExtension.xcframework` and `AppierNotificationContentExtension.xcframework` to **Do Not Embed**.

![](https://files.readme.io/4563f00-manual-installation_notification_extension_target_embed_settings.png)

* * *

## 

4\. Set up the notification service extension

Modify your UNNotificationServiceExtension, then configure your Xcode project settings.

### 

1\. Modify UNNotificationServiceExtension

The required code changes depend on whether you're inherit the Appier SDK's notification service extension class, `QGNotificationService`, or if you want to customize UNNotificationServiceExtension.

If you're inheriting the Appier SDK's UNNotificationServiceExtension (`QGNotificationService`), then open the `AppierNotificationServiceExtension` folder and replace the contents of the `NotificationService.*` files with the following:

Swift
    
    
    // NotificationService.swift
    
    import AppierExtension
    
    class NotificationService: QGNotificationService {
        override func didReceive(_ request: UNNotificationRequest, withContentHandler contentHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationContent) -> Void) {
            super.didReceive(request, withContentHandler: contentHandler)
        }
        
        override func serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire() {
            super.serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire()
        }
    }

Objective-C
    
    
    // NotificationService.h
    
    #import <UserNotifications/UserNotifications.h>
    #import <AppierExtension/AppierExtension.h>
      
    @interface NotificationService : QGNotificationService
    @end
    
    
    
    // NotificationService.m
    
    #import "NotificationService.h"
      
    @implementation NotificationService
      
    - (void)didReceiveNotificationRequest:(UNNotificationRequest *)request withContentHandler:(void (^)(UNNotificationContent * _Nonnull))contentHandler {
        [super didReceiveNotificationRequest:request withContentHandler:contentHandler];
    }
    
    - (void)serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire {
        [super serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire];
    }
    
    @end

Otherwise, if you're using a custom UNNotificationServiceExtension implementation, override the following methods:

  * Swift: `didReceive(_:withContentHandler:)` and `serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire()`
  * Objective-C: `didReceiveNotificationRequest:withContentHandler:` and `serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire`



The following code sample demonstrates one way to override the appropriate methods in your notification extension:

Swift
    
    
    import AppierExtension
    
    class NotificationService: UNNotificationService {
      
      var contentHandler: (UNNotificationContent) -> Void
      var bestAttemptContent: UNMutableNotificationContent
      
      override func didReceive(_ request: UNNotificationRequest, withContentHandler contentHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationContent) -> Void) {
        self.bestAttemptContent = request.content.mutableCopy() as! UNMutableNotificationContent
        self.contentHandler = contentHandler
        
        let isAppierPush = QGNotificationSdk.sharedInstance(withAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID).isAppierPush(request.content.userInfo)
        if isAppierPush {
          QGNotificationSdk.sharedInstance(withAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID).didReceive(request) { content in
            contentHandler(content);
          }
        }
      }
      
      override func serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire() {
        let isAppierPush = QGNotificationSdk.sharedInstance(withAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID).isAppierPush(self.bestAttemptContent.userInfo)
        if isAppierPush {
          self.contentHandler(self.bestAttemptContent)
        }
      }
    }

Objective-C
    
    
    @interface NotificationService ()
    
    @property (nonatomic, strong) void (^contentHandler)(UNNotificationContent *contentToDeliver);
    @property (nonatomic, strong) UNMutableNotificationContent *bestAttemptContent;
    
    @end
    
    - (void)didReceiveNotificationRequest:(UNNotificationRequest *)request withContentHandler:(void (^)(UNNotificationContent * _Nonnull))contentHandler
    {
        self.contentHandler = contentHandler;
        self.bestAttemptContent = [request.content mutableCopy];
    
        BOOL isAppierPush = [[QGNotificationSdk sharedInstanceWithAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID] isAppierPush:request.content.userInfo];
        if (isAppierPush) {
            [[QGNotificationSdk sharedInstanceWithAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID] didReceiveNotificationRequest:request withContentHandler:^(UNNotificationContent *content){
                contentHandler(content);
            }];
        }
    }
    
    - (void)serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire
    {
        BOOL isAppierPush = [[QGNotificationSdk sharedInstanceWithAppGroup:APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID] isAppierPush:self.bestAttemptContent.userInfo];
        if (isAppierPush) {
            self.contentHandler(self.bestAttemptContent);
        }
    }

### 

2\. Configure your Xcode project settings

  1. Go to the project navigator and select the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** target.  
Navigate to **Signing & Capabilities** > **App Groups** , and then add the app group using your App Group ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/c3ed69a-step-4-2.png)

  2. In the project navigator, select the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** target. Under the **General** tab, change the deployment target of your service extension to **iOS 10.0**.

![](https://files.readme.io/47d4f32-step-4-3.png)

  3. Find the `Info.plist` file in the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** folder. Add the following row under **Information Property List** :



Key| Type| Value  
---|---|---  
`AppierAppGroup`| String| Your App Group ID  
  
![](https://files.readme.io/f1f32f5-step-4-4.png)

* * *

## 

5\. Set up the notification content extension

  1. In the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** folder, open the following files and replace the contents of the entire file with the following:



**For Swift:** `NotificationViewController.swift`

Swift
    
    
    import UIKit
    import AppierExtension
    
    class NotificationViewController: QGNotificationContentViewController {
      override func viewDidLoad() {
        super.viewDidLoad()
        // Do any required interface initialization here.
      }
    }

**For Objective-C:** `NotificationViewController.h` and `NotificationViewController.m`

Objective-C
    
    
    #import <UIKit/UIKit.h>
    #import <AppierExtension/AppierExtension.h>
      
    @interface NotificationViewController : QGNotificationContentViewController
    @end

Objective-C
    
    
    #import "NotificationViewController.h"
      
    @implementation NotificationViewController
      
    - (void)viewDidLoad {
        [super viewDidLoad];
    }
    
    @end

  2. Go to the project navigator and select the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** target.  
Navigate to **Signing & Capabilities** > **App Groups** , and then add the app group using your App Group ID.

![](https://files.readme.io/480eb3a-step-5-2.png)

  3. In the project navigator, select the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** target. Under the **General** tab, change the deployment target of your content extension to **iOS 10.0**.

![](https://files.readme.io/f3e2f5b-step-5-3.png)

  4. Find the `Info.plist` file in the **AppierNotificationContentExtension** folder. Under **NSExtension > NSExtensionAttributes**, update `UNNotificationExtensionCategory` and add `UNNotificationExtensionDefaultContentHidden` and `UNNotificationExtensionUserInteractionEnabled` with the following values:



Key| Type| Value  
---|---|---  
`UNNotificationExtensionDefaultContentHidden`| Boolean| `YES` or `1`  
`UNNotificationExtensionUserInteractionEnabled`| Boolean| `YES` or `1`  
`UNNotificationExtensionCategory`| String| `QGCAROUSEL`  
  
![](https://files.readme.io/ea78867-step-5-4.png)

  5. Add the following row under **Information Property List** :



Key| Type| Value  
---|---|---  
`AppierAppGroup`| String| Your App Group ID  
  
`Info.plist` for **AppierNotificationContentExtension** should look like this:

![](https://files.readme.io/dca2e7d-step-5-5.png)

  6. In `MainInterface.storyboard`, remove the default **Label**.

![](https://files.readme.io/dd7b8b1-UI_Label.png)

  7. In `MainInterface.storyboard`, select **View** and change the Background to **System Grouped Background Color**.

![](https://files.readme.io/18f37f9-step-5-7.png)

* * *

## 

Send a test push notification

Build the target and follow the instructions in [Sending Test Notification for iOS](doc:test-notification-for-ios) to verify that the rich push notification works as expected.

* * *

## 

Troubleshooting

See the troubleshooting steps below if you encounter issues sending notifications.

  * Ensure that the deployment target of `AppierNotificationServiceExtension` and `AppierNotificationContentExtension` is set to **iOS 10.0**.

![](https://files.readme.io/50bed25-troubleshooting-0.png)

  * Remove `-ObjC/$(inherited)` if it exists in the build settings of the `AppierNotificationServiceExtension` and `AppierNotificationContentExtension`.

  * Ensure that the same App Group ID is used in all three targets.


![](https://files.readme.io/10d571e-troubleshooting-1.png)

  * Under the **AppierNotificationServiceExtension** and **AppierNotificationContentExtension** targets, go to **Build Phases > Compile Sources** to make sure the following files are correctly configured. If not, click **+** to add the files.

![AppierNotificationServiceExtension Compile Sources](https://files.readme.io/babf7a7-Screen_Shot_2020-12-01_at_3.10.25_PM.png) ![AppierNotificationContentExtension Compile Sources](https://files.readme.io/2d442d3-Screen_Shot_2020-12-01_at_3.10.32_PM.png)

# iOS SDK Overview

Integrate your app with Appier iOS SDK to take advantage of features such as sending push notifications, logging custom user data, and delivering in-app campaigns. This page summarizes the setup steps required to begin using the iOS SDK and all the features it supports.

## 

Latest iOS SDK version

We recommend using the latest iOS SDK for continual updates and feature support. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for details about the latest releases.

Latest Appier iOS SDK version| Supported iOS versions| Supported Xcode version| SDK download (for manual installation only)  
---|---|---|---  
8.6.0| iOS 9 to iOS 18| Xcode 12+| [Objective-C and Swift](https://github.com/appier/appier-ios-framework/releases/download/v8.6.0/AppierFramework.zip)  
  
### 

Version notes

Refer to the following notes for known issues and notable behaviors in certain iOS SDK versions.

Version| Notes  
---|---  
• **v7.35.2 or later** • **v8.0.0 to v8.3.0**|  For apps run on iOS 16.4, displaying an in-app campaign with a GIF as its icon causes the app to freeze.  
**v8.4.0 and v8.4.1**| `getRecommendationWithScenarioId:...` fails to return recommendation results when nested product filters are included.  
**v7.21.0 or earlier**| `notification_displayed` and `notification_received` events weren't flushed from local storage when the app was upgraded from a version using SDK 7.21.0 or earlier to an app version using SDK 7.22.0 or later. Events were only flushed after the first post-update launch.  
• **v7.19.2 or later** • **v8.0.0 to v8.3.0**|  For devices running on iOS 12, the SDK is unable to log events to the server due to compatibility issues between Swift and Objective-C in certain tool versions.  
**v8.0.0 or later**|  The original `AppierFramework` will no longer be supported for rich push notifications.  
**v7.27.0 to v7.32.2**|  Small, Medium, and Full Screen in-app creatives will fail to render or render incorrectly if the creative title or message contains `'`,`"`, `\n`, or any HTML tags (such as `<br>`).  
**v7.20.0 to v7.25.0**| [Method swizzling](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling) is enabled by default to support [LINE user sync](doc:campaigns-getting-started-line-user-sync). Apps using these versions may encounter app crashes due to method swizzling conflicts with third-party SDKs. To avoid crashes, please upgrade to the latest SDK version or [disable method swizzling](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#disabling-method-swizzling).To support LINE user sync without method swizzling, set up [iOS deep link handling](doc:campaigns-getting-started-line-user-sync#sync-via-deep-links).  
**v7.10.0 or later**| `AppierExtensionFramework` is used in the Notification Service Extension and the Notification Content Extension for rich push notifications. The main app target still uses the `AppierFramework` introduced in version 7.0.0. See [Migrating to iOS SDK 7.10.0 or Above](doc:migrating-to-ios-sdk-700) to upgrade from an earlier version.  
**v7.10.0 or earlier**|  The display count for in-app campaigns was incorrectly reset after users upgraded from an app version using SDK 7.10.0 or earlier to an app version using SDK 7.25.0 or later. This caused campaigns to exceed display limits from frequency cap settings and the **Show only once in the user’s lifetime** setting.  
**v7.0.0 to v7.9.0**|  Apps using these versions will receive the following Xcode warning, which can be safely ignored: `ld: linking against a dylib which is not safe for use in application extensions`. This is caused by the Appier iOS SDK using a single framework for both the main application target and extension targets. Despite the warning, apps can be successfully submitted to the App Store and safely released.  
  
* * *

## 

Integration overview

### 

Prerequisites

Before integrating the iOS SDK with your app, prepare the following:

  * Your Appier app ID. Find your app ID on the AIQUA Dashboard under the **Account Settings** page.
  * A MacOS device with the Xcode 12 installed.
  * A physical iOS device running an iOS version supported by the iOS SDK to test push notifications with.



### 

Required setup

Complete the following required setup before using the Appier iOS SDK. Once completed, the SDK will begin logging [default user events and attributes](doc:default-aiqua-parameters) and you'll be able to start using all of the SDK's features.

Step | Description  
---|---  
**1.[ Install the iOS SDK ](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/installing-the-appier-ios-sdk-v2)** |  Import the Appier iOS SDK into your iOS project using one of the following methods: 

  * [ Swift Package Manager ](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/installing-the-appier-ios-sdk-v2#installing-with-swift-package-manager)
  * [ CocoaPods ](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/installing-the-appier-ios-sdk-v2#installing-with-cocoapods)
  * [ Manual installation (Not recommended) ](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/installing-the-appier-ios-sdk-v2#manual-installation-not-recommended)

  
2\. **[Enable Capabilities](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/enabling-capabilities)** |  Add the Background Modes and App Groups capabilities to your app.   
3\. **[Initialize the iOS SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/initializing-the-ios-sdk)** |  Initialize the iOS SDK in your project's `AppDelegate` file.   
4\. **[App Tracking Transparency (iOS 14.5+)](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/app-tracking-transparency)** |  Request user permission to use their Advertising Identifier (IDFA) for improved data tracking with the AppTrackingTransparency framework.   
  
###

## 

Publishing your app

Review the following notes and requirements when you're ready to submit your app to the App Store.

### 

Account deletion

If your app allows for account creation, ensure that your app also allows users to initiate deletion of their account from within the app by June 30, 2022. See [Apple's announcement](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=i71db0mv) for detailed requirements.

### 

App privacy

See [Apple App Privacy](doc:apple-app-privacy) for information required to answer Apple's app privacy questions.

### 

SDK configuration options

The following flags can be set in your project's `Info.plist` file. Please refer to the following table for the default values in each SDK version. Note that if a flag isn't explicitly configured or is incorrectly configured, the default value for the SDK version used by the app will apply.

Configuration| Default value| Notes  
---|---|---  
`AppierAppDelegateProxyEnabled`| • v7.20.0 to v7.25.0: `true`• All other SDK versions: `false`| Set to `true` to enable [method swizzling](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#enabling-method-swizzling).  
`AppierSceneDelegateDeeplinkHandlingEnabled`| • v7.30.0 and v7.30.1: `true`• All other SDK versions: `false`| Set to `true` to enable [universal link handling using the scene delegate](implementing-deep-links-for-ios#3-implement-universal-link-handling).  
  
### 

IDFA for iOS 14.4 and earlier

When submitting your app to the App Store, you must provide information describing how your app uses the Advertising Identifier (IDFA). If your app is only using the Appier iOS SDK, select the following options on the IDFA review form:

  * Select **Yes** for **Does this app use the Advertising Identifier (IDFA)?**
  * Select **Attribute an action taken within this app to a previously served advertisement**. Note that AIQUA doesn't track attribution for app installations.
  * Select **Limit Ad Tracking setting in iOS**.

![](https://files.readme.io/2138ecb-idfa-form.png)

# iOS SDK Overview

Integrate your app with Appier iOS SDK to take advantage of features such as sending push notifications, logging custom user data, and delivering in-app campaigns. This page summarizes the setup steps required to begin using the iOS SDK and all the features it supports.

## 

Latest iOS SDK version

We recommend using the latest iOS SDK for continual updates and feature support. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for details about the latest releases.

Latest Appier iOS SDK version| Supported iOS versions| Supported Xcode version| SDK download (for manual installation only)  
---|---|---|---  
8.6.0| iOS 9 to iOS 18| Xcode 12+| [Objective-C and Swift](https://github.com/appier/appier-ios-framework/releases/download/v8.6.0/AppierFramework.zip)  
  
### 

Version notes

Refer to the following notes for known issues and notable behaviors in certain iOS SDK versions.

Version| Notes  
---|---  
• **v7.35.2 or later** • **v8.0.0 to v8.3.0**|  For apps run on iOS 16.4, displaying an in-app campaign with a GIF as its icon causes the app to freeze.  
**v8.4.0 and v8.4.1**| `getRecommendationWithScenarioId:...` fails to return recommendation results when nested product filters are included.  
**v7.21.0 or earlier**| `notification_displayed` and `notification_received` events weren't flushed from local storage when the app was upgraded from a version using SDK 7.21.0 or earlier to an app version using SDK 7.22.0 or later. Events were only flushed after the first post-update launch.  
• **v7.19.2 or later** • **v8.0.0 to v8.3.0**|  For devices running on iOS 12, the SDK is unable to log events to the server due to compatibility issues between Swift and Objective-C in certain tool versions.  
**v8.0.0 or later**|  The original `AppierFramework` will no longer be supported for rich push notifications.  
**v7.27.0 to v7.32.2**|  Small, Medium, and Full Screen in-app creatives will fail to render or render incorrectly if the creative title or message contains `'`,`"`, `\n`, or any HTML tags (such as `<br>`).  
**v7.20.0 to v7.25.0**| [Method swizzling](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling) is enabled by default to support [LINE user sync](doc:campaigns-getting-started-line-user-sync). Apps using these versions may encounter app crashes due to method swizzling conflicts with third-party SDKs. To avoid crashes, please upgrade to the latest SDK version or [disable method swizzling](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#disabling-method-swizzling).To support LINE user sync without method swizzling, set up [iOS deep link handling](doc:campaigns-getting-started-line-user-sync#sync-via-deep-links).  
**v7.10.0 or later**| `AppierExtensionFramework` is used in the Notification Service Extension and the Notification Content Extension for rich push notifications. The main app target still uses the `AppierFramework` introduced in version 7.0.0. See [Migrating to iOS SDK 7.10.0 or Above](doc:migrating-to-ios-sdk-700) to upgrade from an earlier version.  
**v7.10.0 or earlier**|  The display count for in-app campaigns was incorrectly reset after users upgraded from an app version using SDK 7.10.0 or earlier to an app version using SDK 7.25.0 or later. This caused campaigns to exceed display limits from frequency cap settings and the **Show only once in the user’s lifetime** setting.  
**v7.0.0 to v7.9.0**|  Apps using these versions will receive the following Xcode warning, which can be safely ignored: `ld: linking against a dylib which is not safe for use in application extensions`. This is caused by the Appier iOS SDK using a single framework for both the main application target and extension targets. Despite the warning, apps can be successfully submitted to the App Store and safely released.  
  
* * *

## 

Integration overview

### 

Prerequisites

Before integrating the iOS SDK with your app, prepare the following:

  * Your Appier app ID. Find your app ID on the AIQUA Dashboard under the **Account Settings** page.
  * A MacOS device with the Xcode 12 installed.
  * A physical iOS device running an iOS version supported by the iOS SDK to test push notifications with.



### 

Required setup

Complete the following required setup before using the Appier iOS SDK. Once completed, the SDK will begin logging [default user events and attributes](doc:default-aiqua-parameters) and you'll be able to start using all of the SDK's features.

Step | Description  
---|---  
**1.[ Install the iOS SDK ](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/installing-the-appier-ios-sdk-v2)** |  Import the Appier iOS SDK into your iOS project using one of the following methods: 

  * [ Swift Package Manager ](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/installing-the-appier-ios-sdk-v2#installing-with-swift-package-manager)
  * [ CocoaPods ](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/installing-the-appier-ios-sdk-v2#installing-with-cocoapods)
  * [ Manual installation (Not recommended) ](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/installing-the-appier-ios-sdk-v2#manual-installation-not-recommended)

  
2\. **[Enable Capabilities](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/enabling-capabilities)** |  Add the Background Modes and App Groups capabilities to your app.   
3\. **[Initialize the iOS SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/initializing-the-ios-sdk)** |  Initialize the iOS SDK in your project's `AppDelegate` file.   
4\. **[App Tracking Transparency (iOS 14.5+)](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/app-tracking-transparency)** |  Request user permission to use their Advertising Identifier (IDFA) for improved data tracking with the AppTrackingTransparency framework.   
  
### 

Supported features

After completing the required setup, you can begin using all the features supported by the iOS SDK.

---|---

## 

Publishing your app

Review the following notes and requirements when you're ready to submit your app to the App Store.

### 

Account deletion

If your app allows for account creation, ensure that your app also allows users to initiate deletion of their account from within the app by June 30, 2022. See [Apple's announcement](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=i71db0mv) for detailed requirements.

### 

App privacy

See [Apple App Privacy](doc:apple-app-privacy) for information required to answer Apple's app privacy questions.

### 

SDK configuration options

The following flags can be set in your project's `Info.plist` file. Please refer to the following table for the default values in each SDK version. Note that if a flag isn't explicitly configured or is incorrectly configured, the default value for the SDK version used by the app will apply.

Configuration| Default value| Notes  
---|---|---  
`AppierAppDelegateProxyEnabled`| • v7.20.0 to v7.25.0: `true`• All other SDK versions: `false`| Set to `true` to enable [method swizzling](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#enabling-method-swizzling).  
`AppierSceneDelegateDeeplinkHandlingEnabled`| • v7.30.0 and v7.30.1: `true`• All other SDK versions: `false`| Set to `true` to enable [universal link handling using the scene delegate](implementing-deep-links-for-ios#3-implement-universal-link-handling).  
  
### 

IDFA for iOS 14.4 and earlier

When submitting your app to the App Store, you must provide information describing how your app uses the Advertising Identifier (IDFA). If your app is only using the Appier iOS SDK, select the following options on the IDFA review form:

  * Select **Yes** for **Does this app use the Advertising Identifier (IDFA)?**
  * Select **Attribute an action taken within this app to a previously served advertisement**. Note that AIQUA doesn't track attribution for app installations.
  * Select **Limit Ad Tracking setting in iOS**.

# Method Swizzling in the iOS SDK

Method swizzling is disabled by default starting from iOS SDK 7.26.0. You can enable method swizzling to automatically enable the following LINE-related features:

  * [LINE user sync](doc:campaigns-getting-started-line-user-sync)
  * Logging click events (`notification_clicked` and `qg_line_click`) for LINE campaigns that open your app



* * *

## 

Enabling method swizzling

Enabling method swizzling automatically enables LINE-related functions (LINE user sync and logging click events for LINE campaigns that open your app).

To enable method swizzling, add the flag `AppierAppDelegateProxyEnabled` in your app’s `Info.plist` file and set it to `YES` (boolean value). The iOS SDK implements the following swizzled methods:

  * `application:openURL:options:`
  * `application:continueUserActivity:restorationHandler:`



### 

SDK conflicts

If you enable method swizzling and any other SDKs used by your app swizzle the same methods the Appier iOS SDK swizzles, you will encounter app crashes. Method swizzling conflicts can be identified by error message such as:

  * `Appier [DEBUG] [AIQUA] Appier setAppierDelegate CALLED:`
  * `EXEC_BAD_ACCESS`
  * ` Appier `-[AppierAppDelegate appierApplication:openURL:options]:) `



To resolve method swizzling conflicts that result in app crashes, disable method swizzling in the Appier iOS SDK or in the third-party SDK your app uses.

* * *

## 

Disabling method swizzling

To disable method swizzling, set the flag `AppierAppDelegateProxyEnabled` in your app’s `Info.plist` file and set it to `NO` (boolean value).

Note that if method swizzling is disabled, you'll need to set up [iOS deep link handling](doc:campaigns-getting-started-line-user-sync#sync-via-deep-links) in your app to support LINE user sync.

# [iOS] Migrating to React Native SDK 1.5 or Later

If you are using the Appier React Native SDK 1.4.0 and you are upgrading to the latest SDK version, you need to follow the **Rich Push Migration** instructions below to migrate.

  * Starting from React Native SDK 1.4.0, Appier uses dynamic framework **AppierFramework** to make integration easier.
  * Starting from React Native SDK 1.5.0, Appier uses **AppierExtensionFramework** in Notification Service Extension and Notification Content Extension for Rich Push integration.



From SDK Version| To SDK Versions  
---|---  
1.4.0| 1.5.0 or above  
  
* * *

## 

Rich Push Migration

To migrate your app to Appier React Native SDK 1.5.0, update the following parts of your project:

  * The Notification Service Extension
  * The Notification Content Extension
  * Your project's Podfile (if you use CocoaPods for package management)



### 

Notification Service Extension

  1. [Update the contents of the `NotificationService.*` files](doc:rich-push-notifications-react-native#4-set-up-the-notification-service-extension).

  2. Remove `Appier.framework` or `Appier.xcframework` from **AppierNotificationServiceExtension target > General tab > Frameworks and Libraries**.


![](https://files.readme.io/4e9eef3-step_35b.png)

### 

Notification Content Extension

  1. [Update the contents of the `NotificationViewController.*` files](doc:rich-push-notifications-react-native#5-set-up-the-notification-content-extension).

  2. Remove `Appier.framework` or `Appier.xcframework` from **AppierNotificationContentExtension target > General tab > Frameworks and Libraries**.


![](https://files.readme.io/10de9fc-step_47b.png)

### 

Podfile (CocoaPods only)

If your project uses CocoaPods for package management, [update your Podfile](doc:rich-push-notifications-react-native#installing-with-cocoapods) to include `AppierExtensionFramework`, `AppierNotificationServiceExtension`, and `AppierNotificationContentExtension`.
