# Development iOS SDK Versions

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Apple app privacy changes (v7.32.0 or later)
> 
> In December 2023, Apple introduced [new privacy updates for App Store submissions](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=r1henawx). If you're upgrading to iOS SDK 7.32.0 or later and haven't reviewed the updates, please review [Apple App Privacy](doc:apple-app-privacy) to learn more about how to complete your app's Privacy Nutrition Label.

# 

v8.6.0 - March 13, 2026

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue where in-app pop-up campaigns that failed to display due to invalid system resources still incremented the campaign display count and tracked view-through attributions.
  * Fixed an issue where **Medium** and **Full-screen** in-app pop-up campaigns were larger than designed when they were first displayed. Campaigns were displayed correctly after changing the device orientation or re-opening the campaign.



### 

Changed

  * Retail Media Network features have been deprecated.



* * *

# 

v8.5.2 - January 30, 2026

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue causing elevated rates of fallback results for tag recommendations.



* * *

# 

v8.5.1 - January 16, 2026

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue where in-app campaign floating icons and Floating text creatives covered the Dynamic Island when a device was in landscape mode.
  * Fixed an issue preventing in-app campaigns created using the HTML editor from being scrollable after rotating the device between portrait and landscape mode.



* * *

# 

v8.5.0 - December 19, 2025

### 

New

  * Added support for [retrieving the Appier ID](doc:designing-creatives#capture-appier-ids-in-form-submissions) in Creative Studio lead generation campaigns.
  * Added support for switching between multiple app IDs. Contact your customer success manager to enable this feature.



* * *

# 

v8.4.3 - December 5, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue preventing `notification_displayed` and `notification_received` events from being flushed from local storage when the app was upgraded from a version using SDK 7.21.0 or earlier to an app version using SDK 7.22.0 or later. Events were only flushed after the first post-update app launch.
  * Fixed an issue where the display count for in-app campaigns was incorrectly reset after users upgraded from an app version using SDK 7.10.0 or earlier to an app version using SDK 7.25.0 or later. This caused campaigns to exceed display limits from frequency cap settings and the **Show only once in the user’s lifetime** setting.
  * Fixed an issue where automatic flushing stopped working if the number of locally-stored events exceeded 50. Events only began flushing again after an app restart. Affected versions: SDK 8.3.2 to 8.4.2.



* * *

# 

v8.4.2 - October 9, 2025

### 

Changed

  * Deprecated Personalized Campaigns.



### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue that caused calls to `getRecommendationWithScenarioId:...` to fail to return recommendation results when nested product filters were included. Affected versions: 8.4.1, 8.4.0.
  * Fixed an issue occasionally causing app crashes when the in-app campaign image download fails.
  * Fixed an issue where geofence-related events were logged for geofences not registered by the Appier SDK.
  * Fixed app crashes due to `NSPersistentStoreCoordinator` errors.
  * Fixed an in-app campaign issue where the display delay timer was reset every time the user completed the trigger event, if the event was completed before the campaign was displayed.



* * *

#  v8.4.1 - August 22, 2025 Deprecated 

### 

New

  * Internal enhancements to improve CrossX ad performance.



### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue where images failed to display in push notifications when using a proxy URL for the image source. Affected versions: 8.0.0 to 8.4.0.
  * Fixed crashes for apps upgraded from iOS SDK versions 7.11.0 and earlier to versions 7.12.0 and later caused by encoding and decoding incompatibilities. App crashes were associated with the following error message: `[NSKeyedUnarchiver decodeObjectForKey:]: cannot decode object of class (Condition) for key (NS.objects) because no class named "Condition" was found`
  * Fixed app crashes occurring during SDK initialization and event logging due to data type mismatches.



### 

Known issues

  * `getRecommendationWithScenarioId:...` fails to return recommendation results when nested product filters are included.



* * *

#  v8.4.0 - August 8, 2025 Deprecated 

### 

New

  * Added real-time user event inferencing for recommendation scenarios, allowing results to reflect user behavior more quickly.
  * [`flush()`](doc:configure-batching-for-the-ios-sdk) is now supported in web views.



### 

Fixed

  * Fixed a crash that occurred when fetching new in-app campaigns.
  * Fixed an occasional crash that occurred due to the following errors: `QGSignalHandler`, `[QGUncaughtExceptionHandler backtrace]`, `EXC_BAD_ACCESS KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS`.
  * Fixed delayed logging of default user attributes after calling [`renewAppierId()`](doc:regenerate-user-id-ios#deleting-and-regenerating-ios-users) to regenerate `user_id`. Affected versions: 8.0.0 or later.



### 

Known issues

  * `getRecommendationWithScenarioId:...` fails to return recommendation results when nested product filters are included.



* * *

# 

v8.3.2 - June 20, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue where in-app campaigns using GIFs caused app freezes on devices running iOS 16.4.1. Affects versions: 8.0.0 to 8.2.2.
  * Fixed an issue where the default value of [`flushInterval`](doc:configure-batching-for-the-ios-sdk) was incorrectly set to 0 seconds instead of 15 seconds. This issue was only partially fixed in version 8.0.1. Affected versions: 8.0.0 to 8.3.1.
  * Fixed an issue where the in-app pop up campaign display count (used to enforce the campaign frequency cap) was not incremented if the campaign re-rendered due to new changes made on the AIQUA dashboard.
  * Fix an issue causing occasional app crash when calling [`renewAppierId()`](doc:regenerate-user-id-ios#deleting-and-regenerating-ios-users) and [`flush()`](doc:configure-batching-for-the-ios-sdk). Affected versions: 8.0.0 to 8.3.1.
  * Fixed an issue which prevented events from being logged on devices running iOS 12.



* * *

# 

v8.3.1 - May 29, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue causing duplicate user attribute logging when [setting user data permissions (via the `dataTrackingConfig` property)](doc:ios-user-data-permissions#setting-data-permission-settings).



* * *

# 

v8.3.0 - May 21, 2025

### 

New

  * Introduced new methods for handling key-value pairs sent via push notifications.



### 

Changed

  * In-app inbox campaigns returned by `getInboxesWithStatusRead()` are now returned in campaign priority order. Previously, campaigns were returned in descending order by creation date.



### 

Fixed

  * In apps that delayed SDK initialization:
    * The `notification_clicked` event wasn't logged when users tapped a notification to open the app from the "not running" state. Affected versions: 8.0.0 to 8.2.3.
    * Logged events were stored by the SDK but weren't sent to the server until the app was restarted.
  * [`QGInbox.logEvent()`](doc:in-app-inbox-notifications-for-ios#logevent) was not functional, and failed to log custom events. Affected versions: 8.0.0 to 8.2.3.
  * When invoking [`updateInboxRecordLimit()`](doc:in-app-inbox-notifications-for-ios#updateinboxrecord) for the first time, notifications which exceeded the newly-set limit weren't deleted. Affected versions: 8.0.0 to 8.2.3, 7.6.0 to 7.35.1.
  * The `aiq_cg_received` event (used to track control group users in campaign experiments) wasn't logged when the campaign trigger condition was met after clearing foreground in-app campaigns using [`hideInAppCampaigns()`](in-app-popup-notifications-for-android#clearing-all-foreground-in-app-pop-up-notifications). Affected versions: 8.0.0 to 8.2.3.



* * *

# 

v8.2.3 - April 25, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Under certain conditions, re-triggering in-app campaigns caused an additional duplicate `qg_inapp_toggled` and `qg_inapp_displayed` to be logged. Affected versions: 8.0.0 to 8.2.2.
  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is now correctly logged by the SDK. In versions 8.0.0 to 8.2.2, this event wasn't logged by the SDK.



* * *

# 

v8.2.2 - February 21, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Clicks on custom HTML in-app campaigns caused campaigns to close unexpectedly. Affected versions: 8.0.0 to 8.2.1.
  * The following events were occasionally duplicated for custom HTML in-app campaigns: `qg_inapp_toggled` (when closing campaigns) and `qg_inapp_clicked`. Affected versions: 7.34.0 to 7.35.0, 8.0.0 to 8.2.1.



### 

Known issues

  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

# 

v8.2.1 - February 7, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * In-app campaigns using Creative Studio incorrectly opened universal links in an external browser instead of opening the corresponding page in the app.
  * In-app campaigns using Creative Studio didn't display for apps using SceneDelegate.



### 

Known issues

  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

# 

v8.2.0 - January 17, 2025

### 

Changed

  * Optimized data transmission process to the server.



### 

Fixed

  * In-app campaigns being displayed would freeze when the SDK was reinitialized.



### 

Known issues

  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

# 

v8.1.0 - December 19, 2024

### 

New

  * Added app ID validation for app web views. If your app and website use different app IDs, contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#771204042804020707180503371607071e12055914181a) ) to modify the SDK's app ID allowlist to ensure web data is logged to the correct app ID.



### 

Changed

  * The `model_id` parameter's data type (included in `recommendation_clicked` events) is now sent as a string. If you're logging this event, you'll need to modify your implementation. Please refer to [iOS SDK: Recommendation 2.0](doc:ios-sdk-recommendation-20#tracking-clicks-and-impressions) for details.



### 

Fixed

  * Apps no longer encounter unexpected crashes due to an occasional race condition that occurred when displaying in-app campaigns. Affected versions: 8.0.0 and 8.0.1.



### 

Known issues

  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

# 

v8.0.1 - November 15, 2024

### 

Changed

  * Improved debug logging for in-app Creative Studio campaigns.



### 

Fixed

  * The [default `flushInterval`](doc:configure-batching-for-the-ios-sdk) was incorrectly set to 0 seconds instead of 15 seconds. Affected version: v8.0.0.



### 

Known issues

  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.



* * *

# 

v8.0.0 - October 31, 2024

### 

New

  * Support for Retail Media Network features (beta). To learn more, contact your customer success manager.
  * Support for AiDeal features (beta). To learn more, contact your customer success manager.



### 

Fixed

  * In-app pop-up campaign floating icons are no longer pushed off-screen when the campaign text is too long.
  * Long in-app pop-up floating campaign messages are no longer cut off when the device orientation changes.
  * `qg_inapp_toggled` events are no longer logged when in-app campaign action buttons are clicked. Affected versions: 7.27.0 to 7.34.0.
  * `qg_inapp_closed` events are no longer logged when collapsing an in-app pop-up campaign to a floating icon.
  * In-app pop-up campaigns [disabled via SDK](in-app-popup-notifications-for-ios-sdk#disabling-in-app-pop-up-campaigns) are no longer displayed upon app launch or when the campaign is disabled after a delay setting is configured. Affected version: 7.34.0.
  * Creative Studio campaigns now display every time the trigger event is detected. Previously, campaigns displayed only after the first instance of the trigger event and failed to display after subsequent events. Affected version: 7.34.0.
  * Deep links in Creative Studio campaigns are no longer incorrectly encoded. Affected versions: 7.32.2 to 7.34.0.



### 

Known issues

  * The default `aiq_cg_received` event, which is used to track which users are part of in-app campaign experiment control groups, is not logged by the SDK. As a result, control group users can't be identified for segmentation and campaign experiment performance metrics may be inaccurate.

#  v6.0.0 - May 29, 2020 Deprecated 

  * [New] Support for iOS integration with AiDeal. AiDeal is Appier's AI-powered platform that helps trigger purchase decisions for hesitant customers. [Find out more about AiDeal](https://docs.aideal.appier.com/docs/how-aideal-works).



> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
> Appier iOS SDK 6.0.0 includes **UIWebView** , which has been deprecated by Apple. When uploading your app to App Store, you may receive a warning email from Apple as shown below.
> 
>   * Apple will not accept new apps with UIWebView on App Store.
>   * For apps already on App Store, update is accepted until December 2020.
> 

> 
> **App using iOS SDK 6.0.0 must be upgraded to 7.x.x before November 2020.**

# Stable iOS SDK Versions

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Apple app privacy changes (v7.32.0 or later)
> 
> In December 2023, Apple introduced [new privacy updates for App Store submissions](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=r1henawx). If you're upgrading to iOS SDK 7.32.0 or later and haven't reviewed the updates, please review [Apple App Privacy](doc:apple-app-privacy) to learn more about how to complete your app's Privacy Nutrition Label.

# 

v7.35.6 - October 23, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue preventing `notification_displayed` and `notification_received` events from being flushed from local storage when the app was upgraded from a version using SDK 7.21.0 or earlier to an app version using SDK 7.22.0 or later. Events were only flushed after the first post-update app launch.
  * Fixed an issue where the display count for in-app campaigns was incorrectly reset after users upgraded from an app version using SDK 7.10.0 or earlier to an app version using SDK 7.25.0 or later. This caused campaigns to exceed display limits from frequency cap settings and the **Show only once in the user’s lifetime** setting.



* * *

# 

v7.35.5 - September 19, 2025

### 

Changed

  * Deprecated Personalized Campaigns.



### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue where geofence-related events were logged for geofences not registered by the Appier SDK.
  * Fixed app crashes due to `NSPersistentStoreCoordinator` errors.
  * Fixed an issue where in-app pop-up campaigns didn't display for devices running iOS 13.4 or earlier.
  * Fixed an in-app campaign issue where the display delay timer was reset every time the user completed the trigger event, if the event was completed before the campaign was displayed.



* * *

#  v7.35.4 - September 12, 2025 Deprecated 

  


* * *

# 

v7.35.3 - August 15, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue where images failed to display in push notifications when using a proxy URL for the image source. Affected versions: 7.15.0 to 7.35.2.
  * Fixed delayed logging of default user attributes after calling [`renewAppierId()`](doc:regenerate-user-id-ios#deleting-and-regenerating-ios-users) to regenerate `user_id`. Affected versions: 7.33.1 and later.
  * Fixed occasional app crashes occurring during SDK initialization and event logging due to data type mismatches.
  * Fixed occasional app crashes that occurred when attempting to display an in-app campaign while another campaign was already being displayed. App crashes were associated with the following error message: `NSInvalidArgumentException: Application tried to present modally a view controller <Appier.AIQInAppPopUpViewController: 0x109796d00> that is already being presented by <Appier.AIQInAppWebViewPresenter: 0x10db1bc00>`.



* * *

# 

v7.35.2 - July 18, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * Fixed an issue where in-app campaigns using GIFs caused app freezes on devices running iOS 16.4.1. Affects versions: 7.33.0 to 7.35.1.
  * Fixed an issue which prevented events from being logged on devices running iOS 12.
  * Fix occasional app crashes when displaying in-app campaigns.
  * Fix occasional app crashes when encountering the following errors: `QGSignalHandler`, `[QGUncaughtExceptionHandler backtrace]`, `EXC_BAD_ACCESS KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS`.



* * *

# 

v7.35.1 - February 21, 2025

### 

Fixed

  * The following events were occasionally duplicated for custom HTML in-app campaigns: `qg_inapp_toggled` (when closing campaigns) and `qg_inapp_clicked`. Affected versions: 7.34.0 to 7.35.0, 8.0.0 to 8.2.1.



* * *

# 

v7.35.0 - December 27, 2024

### 

Changed

  * The `model_id` parameter's data type (included in `recommendation_clicked` events) is now sent as a string. If you're logging this event, you'll need to modify your implementation. Please refer to [iOS SDK: Recommendation 2.0](doc:ios-sdk-recommendation-20#tracking-clicks-and-impressions) for details.



### 

Fixed

  * A floating icon was incorrectly displayed when in-app pop-up campaigns using basic creatives with **Notification Persistence** set to **Don 't persist** and were triggered immediately after app launch. Affected versions: 7.33.0 to 7.34.1.
  * The entire screen was incorrectly covered with a gray mask when in-app pop-up campaigns using basic creatives with background overlays enabled were triggered immediately after app launch by events other than `app_launched`. Affected versions: 7.32.1 to 7.34.1.



* * *

# 

v7.34.1 - November 22, 2024

### 

Changed

  * Improved debug logging for in-app Creative Studio campaigns.



### 

Fixed

  * Creative Studio campaigns now display every time the trigger event is detected. Previously, campaigns only displayed after the first instance of the trigger event and failed to display after subsequent events. Affected version: 7.34.0.
  * Deep links in Creative Studio campaigns are no longer incorrectly encoded. Affected versions: 7.32.2 to 7.34.0.



* * *

# 

v7.34.0 - September 6, 2024

### 

New

  * Support interactions with background while an in-app creative studio campaign is displayed. Creative studio is a beta feature. To learn more, contact your customer success manager.



### 

Fixed

  * When in-app creative studio campaigns were triggered, a loading indicator was displayed, blocking the user interface. Creative studio is a beta feature. To learn more, contact your customer success manager.
  * HTML in-app campaigns not displaying in the center when triggered by the `app_launched` event.



* * *

# 

v7.33.1 - September 2, 2024

### 

Fixed

  * After regenerating the Appier ID using `renewAppierId()`:
    * Events stored by the SDK are not flushed.
    * In-app pop-up campaigns being displayed continue to display.
    * In-app pop-up campaigns set to display using time delays continue to display.
  * On apps running SDK 7.33.0, campaigns whose persistence setting is changed to **Don 't persist** display a blank floating icon after the setting change.
  * Medium creatives with long descriptions pushed other creative elements out of the visible area. After this fix, descriptions have a maximum height, after which the description becomes scrollable.
  * Slider and Carousel creatives are not properly resized after rotating a device to landscape mode.



* * *

# 

v7.33.0 - July 19, 2024

### 

New

  * Support for GIF and APNG files for in-app pop-up campaign floating icon images on devices running iOS 13+. On devices running an operating system version earlier than iOS 13, the first frame of the GIF/APNG will be used as the floating icon image.



### 

Fixed

  * In-app pop-up campaigns weren't refreshed if the campaign creative was updated and the app was re-opened from the background.



* * *

# 

v7.32.4 - June 21, 2024

### 

Changed

  * Optimized the SDK's in-app pop-up campaign fetching mechanism to reduce occurrences of unexpected app crashes on app launch.



### 

Fixed

  * Scrolling and zooming were inadvertently enabled for in-app pop-up campaigns. Affected versions: v7.27.0 to v7.32.3.



* * *

# 

v7.32.3 - April 12, 2024

### 

Fixed

  * Occasional app crashes when the app storage I/O is limited. App crashes were associated with the following error message: `__boundsFail: index 199 beyond bounds`.
  * If the device was in portrait orientation, pages that should have been locked to landscape orientation would unexpectedly switch back to portrait mode after closing an in-app campaign.
  * Medium in-app creative messages became scrollable if the message content exceed three lines. After this fix, the creative message can support 15 lines of content before becoming scrollable.
  * Small, Medium, and Full Screen in-app creatives failed to render or rendered incorrectly if the creative title or message contained `'` or `"`.



### 

Changed

  * Remove support for HTML tags (such as `<br>`) and adding line breaks using `\n` in creative titles, messages, and button text.



* * *

# 

v7.32.2 - March 15, 2024

### 

New

  * Support Recommendation for in-app creative studio campaigns. Creative studio is a beta feature. To learn more, contact your customer success manager.



### 

Fixed

  * Image dimensions for in-app campaign **Medium** creatives were improperly rounded, causing image cropping when the campaign was displayed.
  * In-app creative studio campaigns didn't display unicode characters properly. Creative studio is a beta feature. To learn more, contact your customer success manager.
  * When users clicked on redirect links inside in-app creative studio campaigns, the in-app campaign would incorrectly redirect to the destination URL. After this fix, the redirect URL is opened in an external browser, and the in-app campaign remains unchanged.
  * App crashes due to lack of device storage. Associated error message: `Reason:This NSPersistentStoreCoordinator has no persistent stores (disk full). It cannot perform a save operation.`



### 

Known issues

  * Small, Medium, and Full Screen in-app creatives will fail to render or render incorrectly if the creative title or message contains `'`, `"`, `\n`, or any HTML tags (such as `<br>`).



* * *

# 

v7.32.1 - February 23, 2024

### 

Fixed

  * Prevent app crashes caused by memory management issues that occurred during multithreading executions. Associated error messages: `block_destroy_helper`, `__swift_memcpy`, `keypath_get_selector_isCollectLocation`.



### 

Known issues

  * Small, Medium, and Full Screen in-app creatives will fail to render or render incorrectly if the creative title or message contains `'`, `"`, `\n`, or any HTML tags (such as `<br>`).



* * *

# 

v7.32.0 - February 2, 2024

### 

Fixed

  * In compliance with Apple's [new privacy updates for App Store submissions](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=r1henawx), the Appier SDK now provides:
    * A privacy manifest: The privacy manifest includes a property list of all the types of data collected by the SDK, and the reasons for certain API usage. For details, see [Apple App Privacy](doc:apple-app-privacy#app-privacy-manifest-ios-sdk-7320-or-later).
    * Code signing: The XCFramework is now signed by Appier, ensuring that your app is using a secure SDK.



### 

Changed

  * IDFA is no longer collected by default.



### 

Known issues

  * Small, Medium, and Full Screen in-app creatives will fail to render or render incorrectly if the creative title or message contains `'`, `"`, `\n`, or any HTML tags (such as `<br>`).



* * *

v7.31.0 - December 29, 2023

New

  * Support for in-app creative studio. To learn more about this beta feature, contact your customer success manager.



### 

Known issues

  * Small, Medium, and Full Screen in-app creatives will fail to render or render incorrectly if the creative title or message contains `'`, `"`, `\n`, or any HTML tags (such as `<br>`).

# 

v7.30.2 - December 22, 2023

### 

New

  * Introduced a new flag in `Info.plist` for [handling universal links](doc:implementing-deep-links-for-ios#using-the-scene-delegate) for apps using the scene delegate.



### 

Fixed

  * The app’s preferred font face settings weren't applied when rendering in-app campaigns in some languages, such as Japanese.
  * Occasional app crashes occurred when configuring user data permission settings in debug mode. Affected versions: v7.30.0 and v7.30.1. App crashes were associated with the following error message:
    * `swift_isUniquelyReferenced_nonNull_native`
    * `-[QGSdk logUserDetailWithCompletionHandler:]`
    * `keypath_get_selector_isCollectLocation`
  * User data permissions settings didn't take affect during the first app launch after app installation for apps:
    * Using iOS SDK 7.30.0
    * Where the data tracking settings are configured before the SDK initialization
  * Conversions for [deleted users](doc:regenerate-user-id-ios#deleting-and-regenerating-ios-users) were attributed to the click or view completed by the user associated with the previous ID rather than the regenerated ID.



### 

Known issues

  * Small, Medium, and Full Screen in-app creatives will fail to render or render incorrectly if the creative title or message contains `'`, `"`, `\n`, or any HTML tags (such as `<br>`).



* * *

# 

v7.30.1 - December 1, 2023

### 

Fixed

  * Apps upgraded from iOS SDK versions 7.11.0 and earlier to versions 7.12.0 or later crashed due to encoding/decoding incompatibilities. App crashes were associated with the following error message:
    * `[NSKeyedUnarchiver decodeObjectForKey:]: cannot decode object of class (Condition) for key (NS.objects) because no class named "Condition" was found`
  * Apps using iOS SDK 7.27.0 or later occasionally crashed due to a race condition when displaying an in-app pop-up campaign. App crashes were associated with the following error message:
    * `Reason:Application tried to present a nil modal view controller on target <UIViewController: 0x10a61cdf0>.`
  * Apps occasionally crashed when the Appier SDK initialized the log collection mechanism. App crashes were associated with the following error messages:
    * `Fatal Exception: NSInvalidArgumentException`
    * `+[QGUncaughtExceptionHandler backtrace]`



### 

Known issues

  * Small, Medium, and Full Screen in-app creatives will fail to render or render incorrectly if the creative title or message contains `'`, `"`, `\n`, or any HTML tags (such as `<br>`).



* * *

Changed

  * Disabled method swizzling by default to prevent conflicts with third-party SDKs. Method swizzling was automatically enabled in versions 7.20.0 to 7.25.0.
    * If you're upgrading from versions 7.20.0 to 7.25.0 and relied on method swizzling to enable LINE user sync and tracking click events for LINE campaigns via deep link, please configure [iOS deep link handling](doc:line-user-profile-sync#syncing-via-ios-deep-links) in your app or [explicitly enable method swizzling](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#enabling-method-swizzling).



* * *

# 

v7.25.0- May 26, 2023

### 

New

  * Introduced [`getAppierId()`](doc:regenerate-user-id-ios#retrieving-userid), which returns the Appier SDK-generated identifier (`userId`).
  * Introduced [`renewAppierId()`](doc:regenerate-user-id-ios#deleting-and-regenerating-ios-users), which regenerates the Appier SDK-generated identifier (`userId`) and removes all locally cached data associated with that `userId`. Replaces the deprecated `renewUserId()`.



### 

Changed

  * Clicking on an in-app pop-up campaign's **Floating Text** creative without a valid deep link and persistence settings set to **Persist until the notification is click** will now cause the floating icon to collapse without disappearing. Previously, the floating icon disappeared after collapsing.



### 

Known issues

  * Method swizzling is enabled by default, potentially causing [conflicts with third-party SDKs](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#sdk-conflicts).



* * *

# 

v7.24.0 - April 14, 2023

### 

New

  * Support for tag recommendation. This feature is only available through Appier Professional Services. Contact your customer success manager to learn more.



### 

Known issues

  * Method swizzling is enabled by default, potentially causing [conflicts with third-party SDKs](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#sdk-conflicts).



* * *

# 

v7.23.1 - March 31, 2023

### 

Fixed

  * Apps displaying [in-app campaigns using custom HTML](doc:campaigns-in-app-custom-html-editor) occasionally crashed when users clicked on the campaign's [close button](doc:campaigns-in-app-custom-html-editor#for-buttons) multiple times.
  * App crashes occurred while displaying in-app campaigns with images whose URLs included a newline (`\n`).
  * Events which were logged by the SDK but had not yet been flushed to AIQUA were deleted after the app was killed. Starting from version 7.23.1, stored events will be flushed to AIQUA in the first [batch interval](doc:configure-batching-for-the-ios-sdk) in the subsequent app launch.



### 

Known issues

  * Method swizzling is enabled by default, potentially causing [conflicts with third-party SDKs](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#sdk-conflicts).



* * *

# 

v7.23.0 - March 17, 2023

### 

Changed

  * Internal SDK updates to prepare for future multi-data center support



### 

Fixed

  * A race condition which caused unexpected app crashes



### 

Known issues

  * Method swizzling is enabled by default, potentially causing [conflicts with third-party SDKs](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#sdk-conflicts).



* * *

# 

v7.22.0 - February 17, 2023

### 

New

  * Starting from SDK v7.22.0, the following Recommendation API base URL will be used by the SDK: `https://aiqua-intel.prd.c.appier.net`. If your app requires the [Recommendation API](doc:ios-sdk-recommendation-20) and uses an allowlist to specify trusted domains, please add the new API endpoint URL to your allowlist.



### 

Fixed

  * Non-English characters weren't supported inside [in-app campaign image URLs](doc:campaigns-in-app-campaigns-in-app-popup-basic-creatives#image-url).



### 

Known issues

  * Method swizzling is enabled by default, potentially causing [conflicts with third-party SDKs](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#sdk-conflicts).



* * *

# 

v7.21.0 - December 29, 2022

### 

New

  * Support for the [Display background overlay](doc:campaigns-in-app-popup-basic-creatives#background-overlay) option to display or disable background overlay in in-app notifications.



### 

Fixed

  * In-app campaign data isn't refreshed promptly in some cases, causing a slight delay in applying campaign settings. Affected SDK versions: 7.19.0, 7.19.1, 7.19.2 and 7.20.0.



### 

Known issues

  * Method swizzling is enabled by default, potentially causing [conflicts with third-party SDKs](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#sdk-conflicts).



* * *

# 

v7.20.0 - December 16, 2022

### 

New

  * Use [method swizzling](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling) to support syncing LINE users with app users via a LIFF URL or via links embedded in AIQUA LINE campaigns that direct to an iOS SDK-integrated app. For details, see [LINE User Sync](doc:line-user-profile-sync).
    * Method swizzling in the iOS SDK can be disabled. For details, see [Disabling method swizzling](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#disabling-method-swizzling).
    * Method swizzling in the iOS SDK may conflict with third-party SDK services. For details, see [SDK conflicts](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#sdk-conflicts).



### 

Fixed

  * In-app campaigns that target new app users weren't displayed. Affected SDK versions: 7.19.0, 7.19.1, and 7.19.2.
  * Apps occasionally crashed when calling `flush()`.



### 

Known issues

  * Method swizzling is enabled by default, potentially causing [conflicts with third-party SDKs](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#sdk-conflicts).



* * *

# 

v7.19.2 - November 25, 2022

### 

New

  * `isAppierPush:` is now available in `AppierExtensionFramework`. This API allows you to determine whether a push notification was sent by Appier. For usage details, see [Handling Push Notifications](doc:handling-push-notifications-for-ios#handling-push-notifications-from-appier).



### 

Fixed

  * The `#` character in campaign notification deep links was incorrectly encoded, rendering some URLs invalid.
  * `recommendation_impression` events weren't logged in iOS SDK 7.19.1.
  * Calling `getRecommendationWithScenarioId()` without the optional `productId` parameter returned an empty array with no recommendation results in iOS SDK 7.19.1.



* * *

# 

v7.19.1 - October 14, 2022

### 

Fixed

  * `notification_displayed` and `notification_received` weren't logged for apps that were:
    * Using iOS SDK 7.19.0
    * Newly installed by the user (i.e. this bug wasn't present if an app using iOS SDK 7.19.0 was updated by the user)



* * *

# 

v7.19.0 - October 12, 2022 (Deprecated)

### 

New

  * `isAppierPush:` has been introduced to the SDK to allow you to determine whether a push notification was sent by Appier. For usage details, see [Handling Push Notifications](doc:handling-push-notifications-for-ios#handling-push-notifications-from-appier).



### 

Fixed

  * Carousels and sliders wouldn't display properly if one or more images contained invalid URLs. After this fix, carousels and sliders will properly display images with valid URLs and won't display images with invalid URLs.



* * *

# 

v7.18.0 - September 2, 2022

### 

New

  * Support for configurable [on-click behavior](doc:campaigns-in-app-popup-basic-creatives#click-behavior) for in-app pop-up campaign floating icons.



### 

Changed

  * The following API used to log events with multiple event parameter values has been deprecated: `logEvent:withParameters:withValueToSum:withValueToSumCurrency:withConvertedEvent:withAttributionEnabled:`
    * For details about the supported API methods, see [Logging Custom User Events](doc:logging-events-with-parameters-for-ios-sdk).



* * *

# 

v7.17.0 - July 1, 2022

### 

Changed

  * Improved the SDK's event de-duplication mechanism.



### 

Fixed

  * Certain special characters in Recommendation 2.0 request query parameters resulted in a `400 Bad Request` response.



* * *

# 

v7.16.3 - May 27, 2022

### 

Fixed

  * Apps occasionally crashed when calling the following methods on SDK versions `7.15.0`, `7.16.0`, `7.16.1`, and `7.16.2`:
    * `logEvent()`
    * `getRecommendationWithScenarioId()`
    * `renewUserId()`



* * *

# 

v7.16.2 - April 22, 2022

### 

Fixed

  * On older iPhone models (iPhone XS and earlier), tap gestures performed on [in-app pop-up](doc:campaigns-in-app-popup-basic-creatives) floating icons were mistakenly recognized as drag gestures. As a result, floating icons in the expanded state wouldn't collapse after being tapped on.



* * *

# 

v7.16.1 - April 15, 2022

### 

Fixed

  * [In-app inbox notifications](doc:in-app-inbox-notifications-for-ios) weren't being received during an app's first launch post-installation.
  * `nil` wasn't a supported value for the [SDK's user attribute logging methods](doc:logging-user-profile-information-for-ios-sdk). This resulted in the attribute's value not being updated if `nil` was logged.



* * *

# 

v7.16.0 - March 21, 2022

### 

New

  * The ability to [clear all foreground in-app pop-up notifications](doc:in-app-popup-notifications-for-ios-sdk#clearing-all-foreground-in-app-pop-up-notifications) using `hideInAppCampaigns()`.
  * The ability to specify the [floating icon's initial position](doc:campaigns-in-app-popup-basic-creatives#initial-position) in an in-app pop-up campaign.



* * *

# 

v7.15.0 - January 28, 2022

### 

New

  * Support for [filtering audience by events within 24 hours](doc:campaigns-in-app-create#4-filter-audience-by-events-within-24-hours-optional) in in-app campaigns.



### 

Fixed

  * Media URLs without filename extensions (`.jpg` or `.png`) weren't supported for push campaigns.



* * *

# 

v7.14.0 - November 5, 2021

### 

New

  * Transparent backgrounds are now supported for in-app custom HTML campaigns.



### 

Fixed

  * When publishing an app from the latest Xcode 13 release, the **Manage Version and Build Number** option is selected by default. This option sets a single version number for all the app's components (including the Appier Framework and Appier Extension Framework), which resulted in `sdkVersion` being incorrectly set to the app's version rather than the Appier SDK version.



* * *

# 

v7.13.0 - August 12, 2021

  * [New] Support for collecting the hybrid SDK version used in hybrid apps. This is supported in the following hybrid SDK versions:
    * React Native SDK 1.6 or later
  * [New] Support for collecting the SDK type used in the app.



* * *

# 

v7.12.0 - July 15, 2021

  * [New] Support for using `=` operator with event parameters in the trigger rule of in-app campaigns.
  * [New] Support for [filtering out purchased products](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20#optional-step-eliminate-purchased-products-from-results) from recommendation results based on `user_id` in WebView. If you are using custom implementation of WebView, you will need to redo the [WebView integration](doc:custom-implementation-of-wkwebview).
  * [Fixed] Floating bubble (icon image) of in-app custom HTML campaigns remains visible in the overlay background after the campaign is expanded.



* * *

# 

v7.11.0 - June 23, 2021

  * [New] Support for including new app users within 24 hours in "New Users" and "All Users" default segments in in-app campaigns.
  * [New] Support for `first_app_launched` event as trigger rule in in-app campaigns.
  * [Changed] Sequence of event tracking adjusted. When the user launches the app for the first time, `first_app_launched` is now tracked before `app_launched`.



* * *

# 

v7.10.2 - May 19, 2021

  * [Improved] Updated the iOS device model list that maps Apple's machine ID (e.g. iPhone13,3) to product name (e.g. iPhone 12 Pro).
  * [Fixed] Debugging events (`Migration - From NSDictionary` and `Migration - inApp`) are tracked when users launch the app for the first time after upgrading to app integrated with iOS SDK 7.10.0 or 7.10.1.



* * *

# 

v7.10.1 - May 13, 2021

  * [Fixed] SDK sends invalid IDFA (0000) of iOS 14+ users when `setIDFAConsent` is set to true and the user's [App Tracking Transparency status](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/apptrackingtransparency/attrackingmanagerauthorizationstatus) is `NotDetermined`. After the fix, SDK no longer sends IDFA of `NotDetermined` users when `setIDFAConsent` is set to true.
  * [Fixed] Issue where local cache related to the in-app campaign fails to be cleared after the campaign is turned off.



> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Known Issue in iOS SDK 7.10.1:
> 
> Debugging events (`Migration - From NSDictionary` and `Migration - inApp`) are tracked when users launch app for the first time after upgrading. This issue has been fixed in iOS SDK 7.10.2.

* * *

# 

v7.10.0 - April 14, 2021

  * [New] Introduced `AppierExtensionFramework` in Notification Service Extension and Notification Content Extension for Rich Push integration.
    * Starting from iOS SDK 8.0.0, the original `AppierFramework` will no longer be supported in Rich Push integration.
    * See [here](doc:migrating-to-ios-sdk-700) for instructions on migrating to iOS SDK 7.10.0 or later.
  * [New] Support for priority management of in-app campaigns. If a user triggers multiple in-app campaigns at the same time, AIQUA displays the one with the highest priority.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note:
> 
> This in-app priority management feature is coming soon on AIQUA dashboard, and you will be able to configure the priority on AIQUA dashboard.

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Known Issues in iOS SDK 7.10.0:
> 
>   * Local cache related to the in-app campaign is not cleared after the campaign is turned off. This issue has been fixed in iOS SDK 7.10.1.
>   * Debugging events (`Migration - From NSDictionary` and `Migration - inApp`) are tracked when users launch app for the first time after upgrading. This issue has been fixed in iOS SDK 7.10.2.
>

# iOS User Data Permission Controls

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Required SDK version
> 
> User data permission controls are only available on iOS SDK 7.30.0 or later.

## 

Overview

To allow your app to comply with data privacy policies and regulations, the Appier iOS SDK allows you to manage user data permissions for the following types of data:

  * Identifier for Advertising (IDFA): Collection disabled by default starting from iOS SDK 7.32.0. In earlier SDK versions, IDFA collection is enabled by default.
  * Location data: Collection is disabled by default.



You can enable or disable collection for this data at any point in your app's lifecycle, even before the Appier SDK is initialized, and the changes will be effective immediately. For example, you may want to update user data collection settings in the following scenarios:

  * After the app is launched
  * After a user has responded to a data collection consent prompt
  * After [regenerating the user's Appier ID](doc:regenerate-user-id-ios#deleting-and-regenerating-ios-users)
  * After a user logs in or logs out of their account



* * *

## 

`dataTrackingConfig` property

The `dataTrackingConfig` property contains the SDK's current data permissions settings. The default definition for `dataTrackingConfig` is defined as follows:

dataTrackingConfig
    
    
    class AIQDataTrackingConfiguration: NSObject {
      public var isCollectIDFA: Bool     // IDFA collection disabled by default starting from v7.32.0
      public var isCollectLocation: Bool // Location data collection disabled by default
    }

* * *

## 

Retrieving data permission settings

### 

Retrieving individual permission settings

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // Get current settings for IDFA
    let isCollectingIDFA: Bool = QGSdk.getSharedInstance().dataTrackingConfig.isCollectIDFA
    
    // Get current settings for location data
    let isCollectingLocation: Bool = QGSdk.getSharedInstance().dataTrackingConfig.isCollectLocation
    
    
    // Get current settings for IDFA
    BOOL isCollectingIDFA = [QGSdk getSharedInstance].dataTrackingConfig.isCollectIDFA;
    
    // Get current settings for location data
    BOOL isCollectingLocation = [QGSdk getSharedInstance].dataTrackingConfig.isCollectLocation;

### 

Retrieving all permission settings

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    let config = QGSdk.getSharedInstance().dataTrackingConfig
    
    
    AIQDataTrackingConfiguration config = [QGSdk getSharedInstance].dataTrackingConfig;

* * *

## 

Setting data permission settings

### 

Setting individual permissions

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // Enable IDFA collection permissions
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().dataTrackingConfig.isCollectIDFA = true
    
    // Enable location data collection permissions
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().dataTrackingConfig.isCollectLocation = true
    
    
    // Enable IDFA collection permissions
    [QGSdk getSharedInstance].dataTrackingConfig.isCollectIDFA = YES;
    
    // Enable location data collection permissions
    [QGSdk getSharedInstance].dataTrackingConfig.isCollectLocation = YES;

### 

Setting all permissions

To set all data permissions simultaneously, instantiate an `AIQDataTrackingConfiguration` instance and assign it to `dataTrackingConfig`:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    let trackingConfig: AIQDataTrackingConfiguration = AIQDataTrackingConfiguration(isCollectIDFA: false, isCollectLocation: false) // Instantiate an AIQDataTrackingConfiguration instance
    trackingConfig.isCollectIDFA = true // The settings won't be applied since they're not assigned to QG.
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().dataTrackingConfig = trackingConfig // Save the new settings.
    
    
    AIQDataTrackingConfiguration *trackingConfig = [[AIQDataTrackingConfiguration alloc] initWithIsCollectIDFA:NO isCollectLocation:NO];
    trackingConfig.isCollectIDFA = YES; // The settings won't be applied since it's not assiged to QG.
    [QGSdk getSharedInstance].dataTrackingConfig = trackingConfig; // The settings takes effect.

# iOS SDK Web View Support

## 

Overview

Track custom user events and attributes logged from a web page within a web view by establishing a JavaScript bridge between the Appier Web SDK and the Appier iOS SDK. If the web-to-mobile SDK bridge is not established, your mobile app users will be tracked in AIQUA as web users rather than iOS users.

When a web page is integrated with the Appier Web SDK and web view logging has been configured:

  * Web SDK custom user events and attributes are passed to the iOS SDK.
  * Web SDK default user events and attributes are not tracked at all.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> The [Appier Web SDK's default user events and attributes](doc:default-aiqua-parameters) (such as `page_viewed` and `visited`) aren't tracked from within a web view.

## 

Version requirements

Feature| Required iOS SDK version  
---|---  
Web view logging| Requires Appier iOS SDK 4.1.0 or later.  
Recommendation 2.0| Requires Appier iOS SDK 7.8.0 or later.[Filtering out purchased products by `user_id`](doc:filtering-recommendation-results#exclude-purchased-products) from Recommendation 2.0 results is supported in iOS SDK 7.12.0 or later.  
Multiple app IDs  
(iOS SDK 8.1.0 or later)| If your app and website use different app IDs, contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#7f1a0c0c200c0a0f0f100d0b3f1e0f0f161a0d511c1012) ) to modify the SDK's app ID allowlist to ensure web data is logged to the correct app ID.  
  
* * *

# 

Implementing web view logging

Using the `QGWKWebView` class is the recommended approach for implementing web view logging, as this class is continually updated to support new features.

Alternatively, if you have an existing web view implementation and prefer not to migrate your implementation to the `QGWKWebView` class, you can use [custom JavaScript injections](doc:ios-custom-webview-implementation).

## 

Option 1: Initialize `QGWKWebView`

Instantiate a `QGWKWebView` instance with one of the following methods:

  * Swift: `init()`
  * Objective-C: `init()` or `initWithFrame()`



The following example shows how to create a `QGWKWebView` instance:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    var webview = QGWKWebView(frame: view.frame)
    
    // or specify a configuration with:
    // var webview = QGWKWebView(frame: view.frame, configuration: config)
    
    
    // Inside the view controller
    #import "QGWKWebView.h"
     
    // Using initWithFrame:
    QGWKWebView *webview = [[QGWKWebView alloc] initWithFrame:self.view.frame];
    
    // or specify a configuration with:
    // QGWKWebView *webview = [[QGWKWebView alloc] initWithFrame:self.view.frame configuration:config];

## 

Option 2: Use Storyboard or Nib

Add a `WKWebView` object in the Storyboard or Nib view, then change the class to `QGWKWebView` from the identity inspector.

![](https://files.readme.io/65003cd-QGWKWebView.png)

# LINE Segment FAQs

## 

How are LINE subscribers counted in the segment list?

In the segment list, the **LINE Subscribers** count includes LINE users who are following your LINE channel, and excludes those who have unfollowed or blocked the channel.

![](https://files.readme.io/38b9e39-Screen_Shot_2021-12-28_at_6.20.40_PM.png)

AIQUA detects for new LINE followers once a day.

  * The user and subscriber counts of non-default segments are only updated when the segment setting page is edited or resaved.
  * The user and subscriber counts of default segments are automatically updated once a day. Due to the different update time, the **LINE Subscribers** count listed under **`[LINE]` All Followers** may be slightly different from the count listed under **All Users / All Audiences**. You can see the update time under the segment name.

![](https://files.readme.io/819053f-Screen_Shot_2021-12-28_at_6.20.40_PM.png)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Before 2021 April, the **LINE Subscribers** count of the **All Users / All Audiences** default segment and any created segments included LINE subscribers who have unfollowed or blocked the channel. This has been changed.

* * *

## 

Why do LINE segments include web, mobile, email, and SMS users?

After your LINE channel is integrated with AIQUA, AIQUA automatically creates a default segment **`[LINE]` All Followers**. The number of followers in your LINE channel is listed under **LINE Subscribers**.

![](https://files.readme.io/68e94ba-Screen_Shot_2022-12-16_at_3.57.44_PM.png)

If you are running AIQUA LINE campaigns or are using LIFF URL, you will start seeing user counts listed under web, Android, iOS, Email, and SMS as shown below.

![](https://files.readme.io/ceb4e2f-LINE_other_channels.png)

This is because AIQUA can sync LINE users with web, Android and iOS users if the LINE users click on links in your LINE campaigns (Rich messages and carousel templates) and are directed to your Appier SDK-integrated website or app.

If you have set up [LINE LIFF URLs](doc:campaigns-getting-started-line-user-sync#sync-via-liff-urls), users who click on the LIFF URLs can also be synced.

Channels| Reasons  
---|---  
Web Android iOS| The LINE user is synced with web, Android, or iOS users as described above.  
Email| If the synced LINE user has an email address in the user profile, the user will be counted in the **Email Subscribers** in the segment list. Users who have unsubscribed from email campaigns are not included.  
SMS| If the synced LINE user has a phone number in the user profile, the user will be counted in the **SMS User** segment list.  
  
### 

Disable automatic LINE user sync (Web)

AIQUA enables LINE user sync by default. To disable LINE user sync for web, please reach out to your customer success manager.

# Logging Custom User Events

> 👍
> 
> See [Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data) for detailed guidelines on defining and logging custom data.

## 

Overview

[User events](doc:user-data-collection#user-events) are actions that users perform on your app, such as viewing a product or completing a checkout. Logging user events allow marketers to create segments by filtering users based on their events.

To log custom events using the Web SDK, call `appier('event')`:

JavaScript
    
    
    appier('event', eventName, parameters, valueToSum);

Parameter| Type| Description  
---|---|---  
`eventName`| String| See the guidelines on [field names for custom data](doc:custom-user-data#field-names-for-custom-data) for limitations on `eventName`.  
`parameters`| Object| Optional.`parameters` must be a flat JSON object; it can't contain any nested JSON objects or arrays. See the [Data Logging Guidelines](doc:custom-user-data#data-logging-guidelines) for more details and limitations.  
`valueToSum`| Number| Optional. The monetary value associated with this event. Used to calculate conversion value in [campaign performance reports](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-view-performance#conversions).  
  
> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Logging `page_viewed` for single-page applications
> 
> If you website is a single-page application, you'll need to manually log the `page_viewed` default AIQUA event.

* * *

## 

Event logging examples

### 

Logging events (event name only)

The following example logs the `registration_completed` event without any additional parameters.

JavaScript
    
    
    // Log the `registration_completed` event without parameters
    appier('event', 'registration_completed');

### 

Logging events with parameters

The following example logs the `product_viewed` event with the following parameters:

  * `product_name`: `"Brand A Computer"`
  * `category`: `"electronics"`



JavaScript
    
    
    // Log a `product_viewed` event with the following parameters: `product_name`, `category`
    appier('event', 'product_viewed', {'product_id': 'E0238','product_name': 'Brand A Computer', 'category': 'electronics'});

### 

Logging events with `valueToSum`

The following example logs the `product_purchased` event with the following parameters:

  * `product_id`: `"E0238"`
  * `product_name`: `"Brand A Computer"`
  * `category`: `"electronics"`
  * `product_price`: `1000.0`



In addition, `valueToSum` is set to `1000.0` (no currency specified).

JavaScript
    
    
    // Log a `product_viewed` event with the `product_name` and `category` parameters and a `valueToSum` of 1000.0
    appier('event', 'product_purchased', {'product_id': 'E0238', 'product_name': 'Brand A Computer', 'category': 'electronics', 'product_price': 1000.0}, 1000.0);

* * *

## 

Checkpoint: Validating that events are correctly logged

Follow the steps below to validate that your website is logging events properly.

  1. Open your website and complete the action that logs the event.
  2. On the AIQUA Dashboard, click your account name in the lower-left corner and go to **Recent Activity**.
  3. Click the **Web** tab. You should see a list of logged events on this page. It may take several minutes for the event to display on the AIQUA Dashboard.

![](https://files.readme.io/7c1c0c8-Screen_Shot_2021-03-27_at_2.39.09_PM.png)

* * *

## 

Logging `page_viewed` for single-page applications (SPA)

If your website is a single-page application (SPA), you'll need to manually log the default AIQUA event `page_viewed`. For non-SPA websites, this default event is automatically logged by the Appier SDK.

JavaScript
    
    
    appier('event', 'page_viewed', { url: window.location.href });

### 

Using Google Tag Manager

If you've installed Google Tag Manager (GTM) on your website, log a `page_viewed` event when the browser's `history` object is updated. Create a GTM tag with the trigger type set to **History Change** , then use code snippet provided above to log the event.

# Logging Custom User Events

> 👍
> 
> See [Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data) for detailed guidelines on defining and logging custom data.

[User events](doc:user-data-collection#user-events) are the actions users perform on your app. Logging user events enables marketers to create segments by filtering users based on their events.

The iOS SDK provides the following overloaded `logEvent()` methods, which allow you to log custom events, with or without any associated event parameters, `valueToSum`, or `valueToSumCurrency`:

Objective-C
    
    
    (void)logEvent:(NSString *)name;
    (void)logEvent:(NSString *)name withParameters:(NSDictionary *)parameters;
    (void)logEvent:(NSString *)name withParameters:(NSDictionary *)parameters withValueToSum:(NSNumber *)valueToSum;
    (void)logEvent:(NSString *)name withParameters:(NSDictionary *)parameters withValueToSum:(NSNumber *)valueToSum withValueToSumCurrency:(NSString *)vtsCurr;

Parameter| Description  
---|---  
`name`| Required. See the guidelines on [field names for custom data](doc:custom-user-data#field-names-for-custom-data) for limitations on `eventName`.  
`parameters`| Optional. `parameters` must be a flat JSON object; it can't contain any nested JSON objects or arrays. See the [Data Logging Guidelines](doc:custom-user-data#data-logging-guidelines) for more details and limitations.  
`valueToSum` and `valueToSumCurrency`| Optional. The monetary value associated with this event. See `valueToSum` and `valueToSumCurrency`.  
  
* * *

## 

`valueToSum` and `valueToSumCurrency`

Include `valueToSum` when logging an event to track the monetary value associated with the event (e.g. the total conversion value associated with a `checkout_completed` event), and log `valueToSumCurrency` to specify an [ISO 4217 currency code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217#Active_codes).

> 👍
> 
> If the event is [attributed](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution) to a campaign, `valueToSum` will be included in the total attributed value of the [campaign's performance report](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-view-performance#event-attributions).

See the following sections for examples on how to include `valueToSum` and `valueToSumCurrency` when logging custom events:

  * Logging events with parameters, `valueToSum`
  * Logging events with parameters, `valueToSum` and `valueToSumCurrency`



* * *

## 

Event logging examples

### 

Logging events (event name only)

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().logEvent("event_name")
    
    
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] logEvent:@"event_name"];

### 

Logging events with parameters

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    var event: [String: Any] = [:]
    event["num_products"] = "1"
    event["my_param"] = "some_value"
    event["some_other_param"] = 123
    event["another_param"] = 123.45
    event["unknown_param"] = NSNull.init()
    event["empty_param"] = ""
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().logEvent("event_name", 
                                       withParameters: event)
    
    
    NSMutableDictionary *event = [[NSMutableDictionary alloc] init];
    [event setObject:@"1" forKey:@"num_products"];
    [event setObject:@"some_value" forKey:@"my_param"];
    [event setObject:[NSNumber numberWithInt:123] forKey:@"some_other_param"];
    [event setObject:[NSNumber numberWithFloat:123.45] forKey:@"another_param"];
    [event setObject:[NSNull null] forKey:@"unknown_param"];
    [event setObject:@"" forKey:@"empty_param"];
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] logEvent:@"event_name" 
                         withParameters:event];

### 

Logging events with parameters and `valueToSum`

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    var event: [String: Any] = [:]
    event["my_param"] = "some_value"
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().logEvent("event_name", 
                                       withParameters: event, 
                                       withValueToSum: 123.45)
    
    
    NSMutableDictionary *event = [[NSMutableDictionary alloc] init];
    [event setObject:@"some_value" forKey:@"my_param"];
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] logEvent:@"event_name" 
                         withParameters:event 
                         withValueToSum:[NSNumber numberWithFloat:123.45]];

### 

Logging events with parameters, `valueToSum`, and `valueToSumCurrency`

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    var event: [String: Any] = [:]
    event["my_param"] = "some_value"
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().logEvent("event_name", 
                                       withParameters: event, 
                                       withValueToSum: 123.45, 
                                       withValueToSumCurrency: "USD")
    
    
    NSMutableDictionary *event = [[NSMutableDictionary alloc] init];
    [event setObject:@"some_value" forKey:@"my_param"];
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] logEvent:@"event_name" 
                         withParameters:event 
                         withValueToSum:[NSNumber numberWithFloat:123.45] 
                 withValueToSumCurrency:@"USD"];

* * *

## 

Checkpoint: Validate that events are logged properly

Follow the steps below to validate that your app is logging events properly.

  1. Launch your app and complete the actions that log the event.
  2. On the AIQUA dashboard, go to **Settings > Recent Activity**.
  3. Under the **iOS production** or **iOS development** tab, you should be able to see the logged event in the table. Note that it can take several minutes for attributes to display on this page.

# Logging Custom User Attributes

> 👍
> 
> See [Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data) for detailed guidelines on defining and logging custom data.

## 

Overview

[User attributes](doc:user-data-collection#user-attributes) are pieces of information that describe a user, such as their name, city, or date of birth. Logging user attributes to allow marketers to segment and filter users based on their attributes.

To log custom user attributes using the Appier Web SDK, call `appier('identify')` as shown in the following code sample, where `attributes` is the object containing the custom user attributes you're logging:

JavaScript
    
    
    appier('identify', attributes);

* * *

## 

Attribute logging example

The following code sample demonstrates how to use `appier("identify")` to log the following custom user attributes:

  * `email`
  * `first_name`
  * `last_name`



JavaScript
    
    
    const custom_attributes = {
      'email': '[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)',
      'first_name': 'Foo',
      'last_name': 'Bar'
    }
    
    appier('identify', custom_attributes);

* * *

## 

Checkpoint: Validating that custom attributes are correctly logged

Follow the steps below to validate that your website is logging attributes properly.

  1. Open your website and complete the action that logs the attribute.
  2. On the AIQUA Dashboard, click your account name in the lower-left corner and go to **Recent Users**.
  3. Under the **Web** tab, you should see the event. It may take several minutes for the logged data to display on the AIQUA Dashboard.

![](https://files.readme.io/3cf462c-recent-users.png)

# Logging Custom User Events

> 👍
> 
> See [Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data) for detailed guidelines on defining and logging custom data.

[User events](doc:user-data-collection#user-events) are actions that users perform on your app, such as viewing a product or completing a checkout. Logging user events allow marketers to create segments by filtering users based on their events.

The Android SDK provides the following overloaded `logEvent()` methods, which allow you to log custom events and event parameters associated with that event:

JavaKotlin
    
    
    public void logEvent(String eventName)
    public void logEvent(String eventName, JSONObject parameters)
    public void logEvent(String eventName, JSONObject parameters, double valueToSum)
    public void logEvent(String eventName, JSONObject parameters, double valueToSum, String valueToSumCurrency)
    
    
    fun logEvent(eventName: String)
    fun logEvent(eventName: String, parameters: JSONObject?)
    fun logEvent(eventName: String, parameters: JSONObject?, valueToSum: Double?)
    fun logEvent(eventName: String, parameters: JSONObject?, valueToSum: Double?, valueToSumCurrency: String?)

Parameter| Description  
---|---  
`eventName`| Required. See the guidelines on [field names for custom data](doc:custom-user-data#field-names-for-custom-data) for limitations on `eventName`.  
`parameters`| Optional. `parameters` must be a flat JSON object; it can't contain any nested JSON objects or arrays. See the [Data Logging Guidelines](doc:custom-user-data#data-logging-guidelines) for more details and limitations.  
`valueToSum` and `valueToSumCurrency`| Optional. The monetary value associated with this event. See `valueToSum` and `valueToSumCurrency`  
  
* * *

## 

`valueToSum` and `valueToSumCurrency`

Include `valueToSum` when logging an event to track the monetary value associated with the event (e.g. the total conversion value associated with a `checkout_completed` event), and log `valueToSumCurrency` to specify an [ISO 4217 currency code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217#Active_codes).

> 👍
> 
> If the event is [attributed](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution) to a campaign, `valueToSum` will be included in the total attributed value of the [campaign's performance report](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-view-performance#event-attributions).

See the following sections for examples on how to include `valueToSum` and `valueToSumCurrency` when logging custom events:

  * Logging events with parameters, `valueToSum`
  * Logging events with parameters, `valueToSum` and `valueToSumCurrency`



* * *

## 

Event logging examples

### 

Logging events (event name only)

The following example logs the `registration_completed` event without any additional parameters.

JavaKotlin
    
    
    // Log the `registration_completed` event without parameters
    QG.getInstance(context).logEvent("registration_completed");
    
    
    // Log the `registration_completed` event without parameters
    QG.getInstance(context).logEvent("registration_completed")
    

### 

Logging events with parameters

The following example logs the `product_viewed` event with the following parameters:

  * `product_name`: "Brand A Camera"
  * `category`: "electronics"



JavaKotlin
    
    
    // Log a `product_viewed` event with the following parameters: `product_name`, `category`
    try {
        JSONObject productDetails = new JSONObject();
        productDetails.put("product_id", "E0238");
        productDetails.put("product_name", "Brand A Camera");
        productDetails.put("category", "electronics");
        QG.getInstance(context).logEvent("product_viewed", productDetails);
    } catch (JSONException e) {
        // Handle the exception
    }
    
    
    // Log a `product_viewed` event with the following parameters: `product_name`, `category`
    try {
        val productDetails = JSONObject()
        productDetails.put("product_id", "E0238")    
        productDetails.put("product_name", "Brand A Camera")
        productDetails.put("category", "electronics")
        QG.getInstance(context).logEvent("product_viewed", productDetails)
    } catch (e: JSONException) {
        // Handle the exception
    }

### 

Logging events with parameters and `valueToSum`

The following example logs the `checkout_completed` event with the following parameters:

  * `product_name`: "Brand A Camera"
  * `category`: "electronics"



In addition, `valueToSum` is set to `1000` (no currency specified).

JavaKotlin
    
    
    // Log a `checkout_completed` event with the `product_name` and `category` parameters and a `valueToSum` of 1000.0
    try {
        JSONObject productDetails = new JSONObject();
        productDetails.put("product_id", "E0238");
        productDetails.put("product_name", "Brand A Camera");
        productDetails.put("category", "electronics");
        QG.getInstance(context).logEvent("checkout_completed", productDetails, 1000.0);
    } catch (JSONException e) {
        // Handle the exception
    }
    
    
    // Log a `checkout_completed` event with the `product_name` and `category` parameters and a `valueToSum` of 1000.0
    try {
        val productDetails = JSONObject()
        productDetails.put("product_id", "E0238")    
        productDetails.put("product_name", "Brand A Camera")
        productDetails.put("category", "electronics")
        QG.getInstance(context).logEvent("checkout_completed", productDetails, 1000.0)
    } catch (e: JSONException) {
        // Handle the exception
    }

### 

Logging events with parameters, `valueToSum`, and `valueToSumCurrency`

The following example logs the `checkout_completed` event with the following parameters:

  * `product_name`: "Brand A Camera"
  * `category`: "electronics"



In addition `valueToSum` is set to `1000.0` and `valueToSumCurrency` is set to "USD", meaning that the monetary value associated with this event is $1000 USD.

JavaKotlin
    
    
    // Log a `checkout_completed` event with the `product_name` and `category` parameters and a `valueToSum` of 1000.0 with `valueToSumCurrency` set to "USD"
    try {
        JSONObject productDetails = new JSONObject();
        productDetails.put("product_name", "Brand A Camera");
        productDetails.put("category", "electronics");
        QG.getInstance(context).logEvent("checkout_completed", productDetails, 1000.0, "USD");
    } catch (JSONException e) {
        // Handle the exception
    }
    
    
    // Log a `checkout_completed` event with the `product_name` and `category` parameters and a `valueToSum` of 1000.0 with `valueToSumCurrency` set to "USD"
    try {
        val productDetails = JSONObject()
        productDetails.put("product_name", "Brand A Camera")
        productDetails.put("category", "electronics")
        QG.getInstance(context).logEvent("checkout_completed", productDetails, 1000.0, "USD")
    } catch (e: JSONException) {
        // Handle the exception
    }

* * *

## 

Checkpoint: Validate that events are logged properly

Follow the steps below to validate that your app is logging events properly.

  1. Launch your app and complete the action that logs the event.
  2. On the AIQUA dashboard, go to **Settings > Recent activity**.
  3. Under the **Android** tab, you'll be able to see the logged event in the table. Note that it can take several minutes for attributes to display on this page.

# Logging Custom User Attributes

> 👍
> 
> See [Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data) for detailed guidelines on defining and logging custom data.

[User attributes](doc:user-data-collection#user-attributes) are pieces of information that describe a user, such as their name, city of residence, or date of birth. Logging user attributes allows marketers to segment and filter users based on their attributes.

* * *

## 

Using built-in methods

The Android SDK provides the following built-in methods for logging user attributes:

JavaKotlin
    
    
    public void setUserId(String userId)
    public void setName(String name)
    public void setFirstName(String firstName)
    public void setLastName(String lastName)
    public void setCity(String city)
    public void setEmail(String email)
    public void setDayOfBirth(int day)
    public void setMonthOfBirth(int month)
    public void setYearOfBirth(int year)
    public void setPhoneNumber(String phoneNo)
    
    // Methods for logging UTM data
    public void setUtmSource(String utmSource)
    public void setUtmMedium(String utmMedium)
    public void setUtmTerm(String utmTerm)
    public void setUtmContent(String utmContent)
    public void setUtmCampaign(String utmCampaign)
    
    
    fun setUserId(userId: String?)
    fun setName(name: String?)
    fun setFirstName(firstName: String?)
    fun setLastName(lastName: String?)
    fun setCity(city: String?)
    fun setEmail(email: String?)
    fun setDayOfBirth(day: Int)
    fun setMonthOfBirth(month: Int)
    fun setYearOfBirth(year: Int)
    fun setPhoneNumber(phoneNo: String?)
    
    // Methods for logging UTM data
    fun setUtmSource(utmSource: String?)
    fun setUtmMedium(utmMedium: String?)
    fun setUtmTerm(utmTerm: String?)
    fun setUtmContent(utmContent: String?)
    fun setUtmCampaign(utmCampaign: String?)

### 

Example: Built-in method

Use the method corresponding to the attribute you want to log. For example, to log the user's `email` attribute, call `setEmail()`:

JavaKotlin
    
    
    // Sets the user's `email` attribute to "[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)"
    QG qg = QG.getInstance(getApplicationContext());
    qg.setEmail("[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)");
    
    
    // Sets the user's `email` attribute to "[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)"
    val qg = QG.getInstance(applicationContext)
    qg.setEmail("[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)")

### 

Clearing attributes using built-in methods

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Setting an attribute to `null` may result in [unexpected segmentation behavior](doc:custom-user-data#event-parameter-and-user-attribute-values).

  * To clear the value of a user attribute with a built-in method that accepts a string, log `null`.
  * You can't clear the values of user attributes using built-in methods that accept integer values.



JavaKotlin
    
    
    // Resets the user's `name` attribute by logging an empty string
    QG qg = QG.getInstance(getApplicationContext());
    qg.setName(null);
    
    
    // Resets the user's `name` attribute by logging an empty string
    val qg = QG.getInstance(applicationContext)
    qg.setName(null)

* * *

## 

Using custom keys

In addition using the built-in methods, you can also specify which user attributes to log by using `setCustomUserParameter()` and specifying a custom key, where `key` is the user attribute you want to log:

JavaKotlin
    
    
    public <E> void setCustomUserParameter(String key, E value)
    
    
    
    fun <E> setCustomUserParameter(key: String, value: E?)

### 

Example: Custom keys

In the following example, `setCustomUserParameter()` is used to set the user's current `rating`:

JavaKotlin
    
    
    // Sets the value of the `rating` attribute to 5
    QG qg = QG.getInstance(getApplicationContext());
    qg.setCustomUserParameter("rating", 5);
    
    
    // Sets the value of the `rating` attribute to 5
    val qg = QG.getInstance(applicationContext)
    qg.setCustomUserParameter("rating", 5)

### 

Clearing attributes using `setCustomUserParameter()`

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Setting an attribute to `null` may result in [unexpected segmentation behavior](doc:custom-user-data#event-parameter-and-user-attribute-values).

To clear the value of a user attribute with `setCustomKey()`, log a `null` value.

JavaKotlin
    
    
    // Clears the user's `rating` attribute by logging a null value
    QG qg = QG.getInstance(getApplicationContext());
    qg.setCustomUserParameter("rating", null);
    
    
    // Clears the user's `rating` attribute by logging a null value
    val qg = QG.getInstance(applicationContext)
    qg.setCustomUserParameter("rating", null)

* * *

## 

Checkpoint: Validating that events are properly logged

Follow the steps below to validate that attributes are being logged properly.

  1. Launch your app and complete the action that logs the user attribute.
  2. On the AIQUA dashboard, go to **Settings > Recent Users**.
  3. Under the **Android** tab, you should be able to see the logged user attributes under the **Other fields** column. Note that it can take several minutes for attributes to display on this page.

# Managing Android Users

## 

Overview

AIQUA Android users are identified using the Appier SDK-generated `userId`.

  * Retrieving `userId`
  * Deleting and regenerating Android users



* * *

## 

Retrieving `userId`

> 📘
> 
> Retrieving `userId` is only available in Android SDK 7.18.0 and later.

To retrieve the value of `userId`, use `appierId` (Android SDK 7.21.0 or later) or `getAppierId()` (Android SDK 7.18.0 to 7.20.0):

KotlinJava
    
    
    // Android SDK 7.21.0 or later
    QG.getInstance(context).appierId
    
    // Android SDK 7.18.0 to 7.20.0
    QG.getInstance(context).getAppierId()
    
    
    QG.getInstance(context).getAppierId();

* * *

## 

Deleting and regenerating Android users

To delete an Android user's data and regenerate `userId`, for example, when a user modifies their data tracking consent settings, you'll need to complete two steps:

  1. **Delete the user 's data with the[Delete Users API](ref:delete-users)** using their unique identifier from your CRM (`user_id`).
  2. **Regenerate`userId` using the Android SDK**. In addition to generating a new `userId`, calling this method will delete all locally cached data, including events, attributes, and campaigns.
     1. **Android SDK 7.18.0 and later** : Use `renewAppierId()`
     2. **Android SDK 6.8.0 to 7.17.3** : Use `renewUserId()`
     3. **Android SDK 6.7.1 and earlier** : Regenerating `userId` is not supported



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> When regenerating `userId`:
> 
>   * The Android SDK won't renew the app's push token. This prevents users from receiving campaigns before cached data (deleted using the [Delete Users API](ref:delete-users)) is purged from AIQUA's servers.
>   * [User data permissions](doc:android-user-data-permissions) will remain unchanged. Reconfigure the relevant user data permissions after regenerating the user if needed.
> 


KotlinJava
    
    
    // Android SDK 7.18.0 and later
    QG.getInstance(context).renewAppierId()
    
    // Android SDK 6.8.0 to 7.17.3
    QG.getInstance(context).renewUserId()
    
    
    // Android SDK 7.18.0 and later
    QG.getInstance(context).renewAppierId();
    
    // Android SDK 6.8.0 to 7.17.3
    QG.getInstance(context).renewUserId();
